sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第119卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 119
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 119

sentences.zh: 卷第一百一十九

translations.literal: Volume 119
translations.idiomatic: Volume 119

sentences.zh: 【宋紀一】起上章涒灘，盡昭陽大淵獻，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Song Annals 1] Beginning in the year of Shangzhang Tanshen, ending in Zhaoyang Dayuanxian, altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Annals I] From the gengshen year to the jiayin year—a span of four years.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝永初元年（

translations.literal: First year of Yongchu of the High Ancestor Emperor Wu (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu, the founding emperor (

sentences.zh: 庚申，公元四二零年）

translations.literal: gengshen, the year 420 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengshen, AD 420)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jihai, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month, day jihai, the Northern Wei emperor returned to his palace.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐立其子暮末為太子，仍領撫軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，大赦，改元建弘。

translations.literal: King Qin Chiqian installed his son Momo as crown prince, who still held the posts of General Who Pacifies the Army and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad; a general amnesty was declared and the era name was changed to Jianhong.
translations.idiomatic: King Qin Chiqian named his son Momo crown prince while keeping him as General Who Pacifies the Army and supreme commander of all forces; he granted a general amnesty and adopted the era name Jianhong.

sentences.zh: 宋王欲受禪而難於發言，乃集朝臣宴飲，從容言曰：「桓玄篡位，鼎命已移。

translations.literal: The Prince of Song wished to receive the abdication but found it difficult to speak of it; he therefore gathered the court ministers for a banquet and said calmly: "When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, the imperial mandate had already shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu wished to take the throne but hesitated to say so openly. He summoned the courtiers to a banquet and remarked at ease: "When Huan Xuan seized power, the mandate of Heaven had already left Jin.

sentences.zh: 我首唱大義，興復帝室，南征北伐，平定四海，功成業著，遂荷九錫。

translations.literal: I was the first to raise the banner of righteousness, restore the imperial house, campaign south and north, and pacify the four seas; my achievements were manifest, and I was therefore granted the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: I was first to raise the righteous cause, restore the imperial line, campaign south and north, and pacify the realm; when my achievements were plain, I received the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 今年將衰暮，崇極如此，物忌盛，非可久安；

translations.literal: This year I approach old age; my honors have reached such a height that things abhor excess—this cannot long endure;
translations.idiomatic: I am growing old this year, and my honors have risen so high that fullness invites decline—such eminence cannot last;

sentences.zh: 今欲奉還爵位，歸老京師。」

translations.literal: now I wish to return my titles and retire in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I now wish to surrender my rank and retire to the capital."

sentences.zh: 群臣惟盛稱功德，莫諭其意。

translations.literal: The ministers only extolled his merits and did not grasp his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers could only praise his achievements and failed to grasp what he meant.

sentences.zh: 日晚，坐散。

translations.literal: When evening came, the gathering dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: As evening fell, the banquet broke up.

sentences.zh: 中書令傅亮還外，乃悟，而宮門已閉，亮叩扉請見，王即開門見之。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Fu Liang had gone outside and then understood; but the palace gates were already closed. Liang knocked on the gate and asked to be received, and the prince immediately opened the gate and saw him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Fu Liang left the hall and only then understood—but the palace gates were already shut. Liang knocked and asked for an audience, and Liu Yu at once admitted him.

sentences.zh: 亮入，但曰：「臣暫宜還者。」

translations.literal: Liang entered and only said: "Your servant should for the moment return home."
translations.idiomatic: Liang came in and said only: "Your servant ought to go home for a time."

sentences.zh: 王解其意，無復他言，真云：「須幾人自送？」

translations.literal: The prince understood his meaning and said nothing more; he simply asked: "How many men should escort you?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu understood and said no more; he only asked: "How many men should see you off?"

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「數十人可也。」

translations.literal: Liang said: "Several dozen will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied: "Several dozen will do."

sentences.zh: 即時奉辭。

translations.literal: He immediately took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave at once.

sentences.zh: 亮出，已夜，見長星竟天，拊髀歎曰：「我常不信天文，今姑驗矣。」

translations.literal: When Liang went out, it was already night; he saw a long comet spanning the sky and, slapping his thigh, sighed: "I have never believed in astronomy—now I shall put it to the test."
translations.idiomatic: Liang went out into the night and saw a comet stretching across the sky. Slapping his thigh, he sighed: "I never trusted astrology—now I shall see whether it holds true."

sentences.zh: 亮至建康，夏，四月，征王入輔。

translations.literal: When Liang reached Jiankang, in summer, the fourth month, the prince was summoned to enter the capital as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Liang reached Jiankang; in summer, the fourth month, Liu Yu was summoned to the capital to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 王留子義康為都督豫、司、雍、並四州諸軍事、豫州刺史，鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: The prince left his son Yikang as Commander-in-Chief of the armies of the four provinces Yu, Si, Yong, and Bing, and as Governor of Yu, stationed at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu left his son Yikang as commander of military affairs in Yu, Si, Yong, and Bing and as Governor of Yu, with his headquarters at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 義康尚幼，以相國參軍南陽劉湛為長史，決府、州事。

translations.literal: Yikang was still young; the prince appointed Liu Zhan of Nanyang, a staff officer of the Chancellor, as chief administrator to decide matters of the headquarters and the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang was still a boy, so Liu Yu appointed Liu Zhan of Nanyang, an aide in the chancellery, as chief administrator to run the headquarters and the province.

sentences.zh: 湛自弱年即有宰物之情，常自比管、葛，博涉書史，不為文章，不喜談議，王甚重之。

translations.literal: From his youth Zhan had the ambition to govern the realm; he often compared himself to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang. He read widely in history but did not write essays and disliked debate; the prince valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhan had aimed at ruling the realm and often likened himself to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang. He read history widely but wrote no essays and shunned disputation; Liu Yu held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙酉，魏更謚宣武帝曰道武帝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day yiyou, Wei changed the posthumous title of Emperor Xuanwu to Emperor Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day yiyou, Northern Wei changed Emperor Xuanwu's posthumous title to Emperor Daowu.

sentences.zh: 魏淮南公司馬國璠、池陽子司馬道賜謀外叛，司馬文思告之。

translations.literal: The Wei Prince of Huainan, Sima Guofan, and the Marquis of Chiyang, Sima Daoci, plotted to defect abroad; Sima Wensi informed on them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Prince of Huainan Sima Guofan and the Marquis of Chiyang Sima Daoci plotted to flee to a foreign state; Sima Wensi reported them.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主殺國璠、道賜，賜文思爵鬱林公。

translations.literal: Day gengxu, the Wei ruler executed Guofan and Daoci and enfeoffed Wensi as Duke of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengxu the Wei emperor executed Guofan and Daoci and enfeoffed Wensi as Duke of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 國璠等連引平城豪桀，坐族誅者數十人，章安侯封懿之子玄之當坐。

translations.literal: Guofan and the others implicated powerful men of Pingcheng in succession; several dozen families were executed by clan punishment. Feng Xuanzhi, son of Marquis Zhang'an Feng Yi, was to be punished as well.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan's testimony implicated one powerful Pingcheng family after another; dozens of clans were wiped out. Feng Xuanzhi, son of Marquis Zhang'an Feng Yi, was also condemned.

sentences.zh: 魏主以玄之燕朝舊族，欲宥其一子。

translations.literal: Because Xuanzhi was of an old Yan dynasty clan, the Wei ruler wished to spare one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xuanzhi came from an old Yan clan, the Wei emperor wished to spare one son.

sentences.zh: 玄之曰：「弟子磨奴早孤，乞全其命。」

translations.literal: Xuanzhi said: "My nephew Monu lost his parents early; I beg that his life be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi said: "My nephew Monu was orphaned young—I beg you to spare his life."

sentences.zh: 乃殺玄之四子而宥磨奴。

translations.literal: He then executed Xuanzhi's four sons but spared Monu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then executed Xuanzhi's four sons but spared Monu.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬戌，王至建康。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renxu, the prince arrived at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day renxu, Liu Yu reached Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 傅亮諷晉恭帝禪位於宋，具詔草呈帝，使書之。

translations.literal: Fu Liang prompted Emperor Gong of Jin to abdicate in favor of Song, prepared the draft edict, presented it to the emperor, and had him write it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang induced Emperor Gong of Jin to abdicate to Liu Yu, drew up the abdication edict, and had the emperor copy it out.

sentences.zh: 帝欣然操筆，謂左右曰：「桓玄之時，晉氏已無天下，重為劉公所延，將二十載；

translations.literal: The emperor took up the brush gladly and said to those beside him: "In Huan Xuan's time the house of Jin had already lost the realm; I was again sustained by Duke Liu for nearly twenty years;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the brush willingly and told his attendants: "Under Huan Xuan Jin had already lost the realm; Duke Liu sustained me for nearly twenty years;

sentences.zh: 今日之事，本所甘心。」

translations.literal: today's affair is what I accept from the heart."
translations.idiomatic: what happens today is what I accept in my heart."

sentences.zh: 遂書赤紙為詔。

translations.literal: He then wrote the edict on red paper.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote the edict on red paper.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝遜於琅邪第，百官拜辭，秘書監徐廣流涕哀慟。

translations.literal: Day jiazi, the emperor withdrew to the residence in Langya; the officials took leave with bows, and Director of the Secretariat Xu Guang wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiazi the emperor moved to the Langya mansion; the officials bowed in farewell, and Xu Guang, Director of the Secretariat, wept in anguish.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，王為壇於南郊，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Day dingmao, the prince erected an altar in the southern suburb and ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingmao Liu Yu built an altar in the southern suburb and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，自石頭備法駕入建康宮。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, he entered Jiankang Palace from Shitou with the full imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were done, he entered Jiankang Palace from Shitou with the full imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 徐廣又悲感流涕，侍中謝晦謂之曰：「徐公得無小過！」

translations.literal: Xu Guang again wept in sorrow. Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Hui said to him: "Master Xu, are you not going a bit far!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang wept again. Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Hui said to him: "Master Xu, isn't that rather much!"

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「君為宋朝佐命，身是晉室遺老，悲觀之事，固不可同。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "You serve as a founding minister of Song; I am a survivor of the house of Jin. Our grounds for sorrow and joy cannot be the same."
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied: "You are a founding minister of Song; I am a survivor of Jin. Our reasons to grieve and to rejoice cannot be the same."

sentences.zh: 廣，邈之弟也。

translations.literal: Guang was the younger brother of Xu Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was the younger brother of Xu Miao.

sentences.zh: 帝臨太極殿，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: The emperor took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, granted a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 其犯鄉論清議，一皆蕩滌，與之更始。

translations.literal: Those who had offended village reputation and pure criticism were all cleared and given a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: All who had been condemned by local opinion and moral censure were cleared and given a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：昔重華受終，四凶流放；

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: In antiquity when Chonghua received the abdication, the four villains were banished;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: When Shun received the abdication, the Four Evils were banished;

sentences.zh: 武王克殷，頑民遷洛。

translations.literal: when King Wu conquered Yin, the stubborn people were moved to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: when King Wu conquered Yin, the stubborn populace was relocated to Luo.

sentences.zh: 天下之惡一也，鄉論清議，除之，過矣！

translations.literal: The wicked of the realm are one in kind—to abolish village reputation and pure criticism goes too far!
translations.idiomatic: Evil in the realm is of one kind—to abolish local moral censure goes too far!

sentences.zh: 奉晉恭帝為零陵王，優崇之禮，皆仿晉初故事，即宮於故秣陵縣，使冠軍將軍劉遵考將兵防衛。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong of Jin was installed as Prince of Lingling; the honors shown him followed the precedents of early Jin. He was lodged in the old Moling county seat, and General Who Conquers the Enemy Liu Zunkao was sent with troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong of Jin was made Prince of Lingling with honors modeled on early Jin practice. He was housed in the old Moling county seat, and Liu Zunkao, General Who Conquers the Enemy, was assigned troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 降褚後為王妃。

translations.literal: Empress Chu was demoted to princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chu was reduced to princess consort.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以司空道憐為太尉，封長沙王。

translations.literal: Day gengwu, Minister of Works Dao Lian was made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengwu Minister of Works Dao Lian was appointed Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 追封司徒道規為臨川王，以道憐子義慶襲其爵。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Dao Gui was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan, and Dao Lian's son Yiqing inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Dao Gui was posthumously made Prince of Linchuan, and Dao Lian's son Yiqing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 其餘功臣徐羨之等，增位進爵各有差。

translations.literal: The other meritorious officials such as Xu Xianzhi received promotions in rank and enfeoffment according to their deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Other founding ministers such as Xu Xianzhi were promoted in rank and title according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 追封劉穆之為南康郡公，王鎮惡為龍陽縣候。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nankang commandery, and Wang Zhen'e as Marquis of Longyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was posthumously made Duke of Nankang, and Wang Zhen'e Marquis of Longyang.

sentences.zh: 上海歎念穆之，曰：「穆之不死，當助我治天下。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in remembrance of Muzhi and said: "Had Muzhi not died, he would have helped me govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed for Muzhi and said: "If Muzhi were alive, he would be helping me rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 可謂『人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁』！」

translations.literal: One may say, 'When a man perishes, the state is brought to ruin'!"
translations.idiomatic: Truly, 'When such a man dies, the state is laid waste'!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「穆之死，人輕易我。」

translations.literal: He also said: "After Muzhi's death, people take me lightly."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Since Muzhi died, people underestimate me."

sentences.zh: 立皇子桂陽公義真為廬陵王，彭城公義隆為宜都王，義康為彭城王。

translations.literal: The imperial princes were installed: Duke of Guiyang Yizhen as Prince of Luling, Duke of Pengcheng Yilong as Prince of Yidu, and Yikang as Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's sons were enfeoffed: Yizhen as Prince of Luling, Yilong as Prince of Yidu, and Yikang as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 己卯，改《泰始歷》為《永初歷》。

translations.literal: Day jimao, the Taishi Calendar was renamed the Yongchu Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On day jimao the Taishi Calendar was renamed the Yongchu Calendar.

sentences.zh: 魏主如翳犢山，遂至馮滷池。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler went to Yidu Mountain and then to Fenglu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor traveled to Yidu Mountain and then to Fenglu Pool.

sentences.zh: 聞上受禪，驛召崔浩告之曰：「卿往年之言驗矣，朕於今日始信天道。」

translations.literal: On hearing that the emperor above had received the abdication, he summoned Cui Hao by post and told him: "Your words of years past have been fulfilled; only today do I begin to believe in the Way of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Liu Yu had taken the throne, he summoned Cui Hao by courier and said: "What you said years ago has come true—only today do I believe in Heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁酉，魏主如五原。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingyou, the Wei ruler went to Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day dingyou, the Wei emperor went to Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔以涼公歆為都督高昌等七郡諸軍事、征西將軍、酒泉公；

translations.literal: Day jiachen, an edict appointed Duke of Liang Xin as Commander-in-Chief of the armies of the seven commanderies including Gaochang, General Who Conquers the West, and Duke of Jiuquan;
translations.idiomatic: On day jiachen an edict named Duke of Liang Xin commander of military affairs in the seven commanderies including Gaochang, General Who Conquers the West, and Duke of Jiuquan;

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐為安西大將軍。

translations.literal: and King Qin Chiqian as Grand General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: and King Qin Chiqian Grand General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史杜慧度擊林邑，大破之，所殺過半。

translations.literal: Du Huidu, Governor of Jiaozhou, attacked Linyi and routed it; more than half were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu, Governor of Jiaozhou, attacked Linyi and crushed it, killing more than half the enemy.

sentences.zh: 林邑乞降，前後為所鈔掠者皆遣還。

translations.literal: Linyi begged to surrender; all who had been seized in earlier raids were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi sued for peace and returned everyone taken in earlier raids.

sentences.zh: 慧度在交州，為政纖密，一如治家，吏民畏而愛之，城門夜開，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Huidu governed Jiaozhou with meticulous care, as if managing a household; officials and people feared yet loved him; the city gates were left open at night and nothing was picked up on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaozhou Huidu governed with household thoroughness; officials and commoners feared yet loved him; the gates stood open at night and no one picked up lost goods on the roads.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主如雲中。

translations.literal: Day dingwei, the Wei ruler went to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingwei the Wei emperor went to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜欲伐涼，先引兵攻秦浩亹；

translations.literal: King of Hexi Meng Xun wished to attack Liang and first led troops against Qin Haowan;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun, King of Hexi, planned to attack Liang and first marched against Qin's Haowan;

sentences.zh: 既至，潛師還屯川巖。

translations.literal: when he arrived, he secretly withdrew his army and encamped at Chuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: but on arrival he secretly withdrew and encamped at Chuanyan.

sentences.zh: 涼公歆欲乘虛襲張掖；

translations.literal: Duke of Liang Xin wished to take advantage of the opening to strike Zhangye;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Liang Xin wanted to strike Zhangye while Meng Xun was away;

sentences.zh: 宋繇、張體順切諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Song Yao and Zhang Tishun remonstrated urgently but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao and Zhang Tishun urged him strongly, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 太后尹氏謂歆曰：「汝新造之國。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lady Yin said to Xin: "Your state is newly founded.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lady Yin told Xin: "Your realm is newly founded.

sentences.zh: 地狹民希，自守猶懼不足，何暇伐人！

translations.literal: The land is narrow and the people few; you can scarcely hold your own—how have you leisure to attack others!
translations.idiomatic: Your territory is small and your people few—you can barely defend yourselves. How can you spare strength to attack others!

sentences.zh: 先王臨終，殷勤戒汝：深慎用兵，保境寧民，以俟天時。

translations.literal: On his deathbed the former king earnestly admonished you: use the army with the utmost caution, keep the borders secure and the people at peace, and await Heaven's time.
translations.idiomatic: Your father on his deathbed urged you earnestly: use force with utmost caution, keep your borders secure and your people at peace, and await Heaven's hour.

sentences.zh: 言猶在耳，奈何棄這！

translations.literal: His words are still in our ears—how can you cast them aside!
translations.idiomatic: His words are still in our ears—how can you cast them aside!

sentences.zh: 蒙遜善用兵，非汝之敵，數年以來，常有兼併之志。

translations.literal: Meng Xun is skilled in war and no match for you; for years he has harbored the ambition to annex you.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun is a skilled commander and not your equal; for years he has aimed to swallow your state.

sentences.zh: 汝國雖小，足為善政，修德養民，靜以待之。

translations.literal: Though your state is small, it is enough for good government: cultivate virtue, nourish the people, and wait quietly.
translations.idiomatic: Though your realm is small, it is enough for good government—cultivate virtue, nourish the people, and wait in quiet.

sentences.zh: 彼若昏暴，民將歸汝；

translations.literal: If he is brutal and tyrannical, the people will come to you;
translations.idiomatic: If he turns brutal, the people will come to you;

sentences.zh: 若其休明，汝將事之。

translations.literal: if he is enlightened, you will serve him.
translations.idiomatic: if he proves enlightened, you will serve him.

sentences.zh: 豈得輕為舉動，僥冀非望！

translations.literal: How can you lightly take action and hope for what is not your due!
translations.idiomatic: How can you act rashly and hope for what is not yours!

sentences.zh: 以吾觀之，非但喪師，殆將亡國！」

translations.literal: In my view you will not only lose your army—you will likely lose your state!"
translations.idiomatic: In my view you will not only lose your army—you will likely lose your state!"

sentences.zh: 亦不聽。

translations.literal: He still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He still would not listen.

sentences.zh: 宋繇歎曰：「今茲大事去矣！」

translations.literal: Song Yao sighed: "This year the great affair is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao sighed: "The great cause is lost this year!"

sentences.zh: 歆將步騎三萬東出。

translations.literal: Xin led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Xin marched east with thirty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞之，曰：「歆已入吾術中，然聞吾旋師，必不敢前。」

translations.literal: When Meng Xun heard this, he said: "Xin has already fallen into my stratagem; yet when he hears that I am turning back, he will surely not advance."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun heard and said: "Xin has walked into my trap; but when he hears I am turning back, he will surely not advance."

sentences.zh: 乃露布西境，雲已克浩亹，將進攻黃谷。

translations.literal: He then posted a public notice in the western borderlands saying he had taken Haowan and would advance on Huanggu.
translations.idiomatic: He posted a bulletin in the western marches claiming he had taken Haowan and would advance on Huanggu.

sentences.zh: 歆聞之，喜，進入都瀆澗，蒙遜引兵擊之，戰於懷城，歆大敗。

translations.literal: When Xin heard this he was pleased and advanced into Dudu Ravine. Meng Xun led troops against him; they fought at Huaicheng and Xin was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xin heard this with delight and pushed into Dudu Ravine. Meng Xun struck him at Huaicheng and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 或勸歆還保酒泉，歆曰：「吾違老母之言以取敗，不殺此胡，何面目復見我母！」

translations.literal: Some urged Xin to withdraw and hold Jiuquan. Xin said: "I went against my old mother's words and brought defeat—if I do not kill this barbarian, what face have I to see my mother again!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Xin to fall back on Jiuquan. He said: "I ignored my mother's counsel and brought defeat—if I do not kill this barbarian, what face can I show my mother!"

sentences.zh: 遂勒兵戰於蓼泉，為蒙遜所殺。

translations.literal: He then led his troops to fight at Liaoquan and was killed by Meng Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his men to fight at Liaoquan and was killed by Meng Xun.

sentences.zh: 歆弟酒泉太守翻、新城太守預、領羽林右監密、左將軍眺、右將軍亮西奔敦煌。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brothers Fan, Governor of Jiuquan; Yu, Governor of Xincheng; Mi, Director of the Right Wing of the Feathered Forest; Tiao, General of the Left; and Liang, General of the Right, fled west to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's brothers Fan (Governor of Jiuquan), Yu (Governor of Xincheng), Mi (Director of the Right Wing of the Feathered Forest), Tiao (General of the Left), and Liang (General of the Right) fled west to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜入酒泉，禁侵掠，土民安堵。

translations.literal: Meng Xun entered Jiuquan, forbade pillaging, and the local people were settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun entered Jiuquan, forbade looting, and the people lived undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 以宋繇為吏部郎中，委之選舉；

translations.literal: He appointed Song Yao Director in the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted him with selections;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Song Yao Director in the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted appointments to him;

sentences.zh: 涼之舊臣有才望者，鹹禮而且之。

translations.literal: former Liang ministers of talent and reputation were all honored and retained.
translations.idiomatic: and honored and retained every talented former Liang minister of standing.

sentences.zh: 以其子牧犍為灑泉太守。

translations.literal: He made his son Mujian Governor of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He made his son Mujian Governor of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守李恂，翻之弟也，與翻等棄敦煌奔北山。

translations.literal: Li Xun, Governor of Dunhuang and Fan's younger brother, abandoned Dunhuang with Fan and the others and fled to the northern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, Governor of Dunhuang and Fan's younger brother, abandoned Dunhuang with Fan and the others and fled to the northern mountains.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜以索嗣之子元緒行敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Meng Xun appointed Yuanxu, son of Suo Si, acting Governor of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun appointed Yuanxu, son of Suo Si, acting Governor of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜還姑臧，見涼太后尹氏而勞之，尹氏曰：「李氏為胡所滅，知復何言！」

translations.literal: Meng Xun returned to Guzang, saw Empress Dowager Yin of Liang and comforted her. Lady Yin said: "The house of Li has been destroyed by barbarians—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun returned to Guzang, visited Empress Dowager Yin of Liang, and offered condolences. Lady Yin said: "The Li house has been destroyed by barbarians—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 或謂尹氏曰：「今母子之命在人掌握，奈何傲之！

translations.literal: Someone said to Lady Yin: "Now mother and son hold their lives in another's hand—how can you be so proud!
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Lady Yin: "Mother and son now hold their lives in another's hand—how can you be so defiant!

sentences.zh: 且國亡子死，曾無憂色，何也？」

translations.literal: Moreover, your state is lost and your son is dead—yet you show no grief. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Your state is lost and your son is dead, yet you show no sorrow—why?"

sentences.zh: 尹氏曰：「存亡死生，皆有天命，奈何更如凡人，為兒女子之悲乎！

translations.literal: Lady Yin said: "Survival and destruction, life and death—all lie in Heaven's mandate. Why act like an ordinary person and grieve like women and children!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin said: "Whether one lives or dies is Heaven's decree—why act like ordinary folk and weep like women and children!

sentences.zh: 吾老婦人，國亡家破，豈可復惜餘生，為人臣妝乎！

translations.literal: I am an old woman; state and house are ruined—how can I still cherish what life remains and dress myself as someone's subject!
translations.idiomatic: I am an old woman whose state and house are ruined—why should I cling to life or play the dutiful subject!

sentences.zh: 惟速死為幸耳。」

translations.literal: Only a swift death would be a blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Only a quick death would be a mercy."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜嘉而赦之，娶其女為牧犍婦。

translations.literal: Meng Xun admired this and spared her, marrying her daughter to Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun admired her spirit and spared her, giving his daughter to Mujian in marriage.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛未，追謚妃臧氏為敬皇后。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day xinwei, Consort Zang was posthumously given the temple name Empress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day xinwei, Consort Zang was posthumously honored as Empress Jing.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，立王太子義符為皇太子。

translations.literal: Day guiyou, Crown Prince Yifu was installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On day guiyou Crown Prince Yifu was named heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬午，詔晉帝諸陵悉署守衛。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day renwu, an edict ordered guards posted at all tombs of Jin emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on day renwu, an edict placed guards at all Jin imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦振武將軍王基等襲河西王蒙遜胡園戍，俘二千餘人而還。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Qin's General Who Inspires Martial Valor Wang Ji and others raided King of Hexi Meng Xun's garrison at Huyuan, took more than two thousand captives, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Qin's General Who Inspires Martial Valor Wang Ji and others raided Meng Xun's garrison at Huyuan, captured more than two thousand men, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李恂在敦煌在惠政。

translations.literal: Li Xun was in Dunhuang and governed with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun was in Dunhuang and governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 索元緒粗險好殺，大失人和。

translations.literal: Suo Yuanxu was coarse, ruthless, and fond of killing, and greatly lost the people's support.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Yuanxu was brutal and bloodthirsty and lost the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 郡人宋承、張弘信招恂。

translations.literal: Song Cheng and Zhang Hongxin of the commandery invited Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Song Cheng and Zhang Hongxin of the commandery invited Li Xun back.

sentences.zh: 冬，恂帥數十騎入敦煌，元緒東奔涼興。

translations.literal: In winter Xun led several dozen horsemen into Dunhuang; Yuanxu fled east to Liangxing.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Li Xun entered Dunhuang with several dozen horsemen while Yuanxu fled east to Liangxing.

sentences.zh: 承等推恂為冠軍將軍、涼州刺史，改元永建。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others installed Xun as General Who Conquers the Enemy and Governor of Liang, and changed the era name to Yongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and the others made Li Xun General Who Conquers the Enemy and Governor of Liang and adopted the era name Yongjian.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜遣世子政德攻敦煌，恂閉城不戰。

translations.literal: King of Hexi Meng Xun sent his heir Zhengde to attack Dunhuang; Xun closed the city and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun sent his heir Zhengde against Dunhuang; Li Xun shut the gates and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁亥，可城羌酋狄溫子帥三千餘家降魏。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dinghai, Di Wenzi, Qiang chieftain of Kecheng, led more than three thousand households to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day dinghai, the Qiang chieftain Di Wenzi of Kecheng led more than three thousand households in surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏姚夫人卒，追謚昭哀皇后。

translations.literal: This year Lady Yao of Wei died and was posthumously given the temple name Empress Zhao'ai.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lady Yao of Wei died and was posthumously honored as Empress Zhao'ai.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝永初二年（

translations.literal: Second year of Yongchu of the High Ancestor Emperor Wu (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu, the founding emperor (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元四二一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, the year 421 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinyou, AD 421)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：夫郊祀天地，修歲事也。

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: Sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars is the fulfillment of the year's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: Sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars fulfills the year's rites.

sentences.zh: 赦彼有罪，夫何為哉！

translations.literal: To pardon the guilty—what is the point of that!
translations.idiomatic: To pardon criminals at such a time—what is the point!

sentences.zh: 以揚州刺史廬陵王義真為司徒，尚書僕射徐羨之為尚書令、揚州刺史，中書令傅亮為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Yizhen, Governor of Yangzhou, was made Minister over the Masses; Vice Minister of the Secretariat Xu Xianzhi was made Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Yangzhou; Director of the Secretariat Fu Liang was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luling Yizhen was made Minister over the Masses; Xu Xianzhi became Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Yangzhou; Fu Liang became Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主行如公陽。

translations.literal: Day xinwei, the Wei ruler traveled to Gongyang.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinwei the Wei emperor traveled to Gongyang.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜帥眾二萬攻李恂於敦煌。

translations.literal: King of Hexi Meng Xun led twenty thousand men to attack Li Xun at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun led twenty thousand men to attack Li Xun at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐遣征北將軍木弈干、輔國將軍元基攻上邽，遇霖雨而還。

translations.literal: King Qin Chiqian sent General Who Conquers the North Muyigan and General Who Supports the State Yuanji to attack Shanggui; they met heavy rain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: King Qin Chiqian sent Muyigan, General Who Conquers the North, and Yuanji, General Who Supports the State, against Shanggui, but heavy rains forced them back.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲子，魏陽平王熙卒。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiazi, Prince of Yangping Xi of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day jiazi, Prince of Yangping Xi of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 魏主發代者六千人築苑，東包白登，週三十餘里。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler mobilized six thousand men from Dai to build a park, enclosing Baideng on the east, more than thirty li in circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor mobilized six thousand men from Dai to build a park enclosing Baideng on the east, more than thirty li around.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜築堤壅水以灌敦煌；

translations.literal: King of Hexi Meng Xun built dikes to dam water and flood Dunhuang;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun built dikes to dam the waters and flood Dunhuang;

sentences.zh: 李恂乞降，不許。

translations.literal: Li Xun begged to surrender but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun sued for surrender but was refused.

sentences.zh: 恂將宋承等舉城降。

translations.literal: Xun's generals Song Cheng and others surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun's generals Song Cheng and others surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 恂自殺。

translations.literal: Xun killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun killed himself.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜屠其城，獲恂弟子寶，囚於姑臧。

translations.literal: Meng Xun sacked the city, captured Xun's nephew Bao, and imprisoned him at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun sacked the city, seized Li Xun's nephew Bao, and imprisoned him at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 於是西域諸國皆詣蒙遜稱臣朝貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the states of the Western Regions came to Meng Xun to declare themselves subjects and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the states of the Western Regions all came to Meng Xun as subjects bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己卯朔，詔所在淫祠自蔣子文以下皆除之；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day jimao, an edict ordered that improper shrines from Jiang Ziwen downward be abolished everywhere;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day jimao, an edict abolished improper shrines from Jiang Ziwen downward throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 其先賢及以勳德立祠者，不在此例。

translations.literal: shrines to former sages and those erected for merit and virtue were not included.
translations.idiomatic: shrines to former sages and those erected for merit were excepted.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王阿柴遣使降秦，秦王熾磐以阿柴為征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、安州牧、白蘭王。

translations.literal: King Achai of Tuyuhun sent envoys to surrender to Qin; King Qin Chiqian made Achai Grand General Who Conquers the West, Holder of the Grand Precedence, Governor of Anzhou, and King of Bailan.
translations.idiomatic: King Achai of Tuyuhun sent envoys to submit to Qin; King Qin Chiqian made him Grand General Who Conquers the West, Holder of the Grand Precedence, Governor of Anzhou, and King of Bailan.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙酉，魏主北巡至蟠羊山。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day yiyou, the Wei ruler toured north to Panyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day yiyou, the Wei emperor toured north to Panyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，西巡至河。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, he toured west to the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, he toured west to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜遣右衛將軍沮渠鄯善、建節將軍沮渠苟生帥眾七千伐秦。

translations.literal: King of Hexi Meng Xun sent General of the Right Guard Juqu Shanshan and General Who Establishes the Standard Juqu Gousheng with seven thousand men to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun sent Juqu Shanshan, General of the Right Guard, and Juqu Gousheng, General Who Establishes the Standard, with seven thousand men against Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐遣征北將軍木弈乾等師步騎五千拒之，敗鄯善等於五澗，虜苟生，斬首二千而還。

translations.literal: King Qin Chiqian sent General Who Conquers the North Muyigan and others with five thousand infantry and cavalry to resist them; they defeated Shanshan and the others at Wujian, captured Gousheng, took two thousand heads, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: King Qin Chiqian sent Muyigan with five thousand foot and horse to meet them, routed Shanshan at Wujian, captured Gousheng, took two thousand heads, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以毒酒一甕授前琅邪郎中令張偉，使鴆零陵王，偉歎曰：「鴆君以求生，不如死！」

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had given a jar of poisoned wine to Zhang Wei, former Director of Langya, and ordered him to poison the Prince of Lingling. Wei sighed: "To poison one's lord in order to live—better to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor gave Zhang Wei, former Director of Langya, a jar of poisoned wine and ordered him to poison the Prince of Lingling. Wei sighed: "To poison one's lord to save oneself—better to die!"

sentences.zh: 乃於道自飲而卒。

translations.literal: He then drank it on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank it on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 偉，邵之兄也。

translations.literal: Wei was the elder brother of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was the elder brother of Shao.

sentences.zh: 太常褚秀之、侍中褚淡之，皆王之妃兄也。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Chu Xiuzhi and Attendant-in-Ordinary Chu Danzhi were both elder brothers of the prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xiuzhi, Minister of Ceremonies, and Chu Danzhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary, were both brothers of the prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 王每生男，帝輒令秀之兄弟方便殺之。

translations.literal: Whenever the prince had a son, the emperor would have the Chu brothers find a convenient way to kill the child.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince had a son, the emperor had the Chu brothers find a way to kill the child.

sentences.zh: 王自遜位，深慮禍及，與褚妃共處一室，自煮食於床前，飲食所資，皆出褚妃，故宋人莫得伺其隙。

translations.literal: After the prince had abdicated he deeply feared harm would reach him; he shared one room with Lady Chu, cooked his food before the bed, and all he ate and drank came from Lady Chu, so the men of Song could find no opening.
translations.idiomatic: After his abdication the prince lived in constant fear; he shared one room with Lady Chu, cooked at his bedside, and ate only what she provided, so the Song agents found no opening.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝令淡之與兄右衛將軍叔度往視妃，妃出就別室相見。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the emperor ordered Danzhi and his elder brother, General of the Right Guard Shudu, to visit the consort; she came out to a separate room to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor sent Danzhi and his brother Shudu, General of the Right Guard, to visit the consort; she met them in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 兵人逾垣而入，進藥於王。

translations.literal: Soldiers climbed the wall and entered, presenting the drug to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers scaled the wall, entered, and presented poison to the prince.

sentences.zh: 王不肯飲，曰：「佛教，自殺者不復得人身。」

translations.literal: The prince refused to drink and said: "In Buddhism, one who commits suicide cannot again obtain a human body."
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused and said: "In Buddhism, one who kills himself cannot be reborn human."

sentences.zh: 兵人以被掩殺之。

translations.literal: The soldiers smothered him with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers smothered him with a quilt.

sentences.zh: 帝帥百官臨於朝堂三日。

translations.literal: The emperor led the officials in mourning at the court hall for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led the officials in mourning at court for three days.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: Day gengxu, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengxu the Wei emperor returned to his palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，詔以河西王蒙遜為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jihai, an edict appointed King of Hexi Meng Xun Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Holder of the Grand Precedence, and Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day jihai, an edict made Meng Xun Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Holder of the Grand Precedence, and Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏主如代。

translations.literal: Day jihai, the Wei ruler went to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai the Wei emperor went to Dai.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，葬晉恭帝於沖平陵，帝帥百官瞻送。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day xinhai, Emperor Gong of Jin was buried at Chongping Mausoleum; the emperor led the officials to escort the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day xinhai, Emperor Gong of Jin was buried at Chongping Mausoleum; the emperor led the officials to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙申，魏主西巡，至雲中。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bingshen, the Wei ruler toured west to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day bingshen, the Wei emperor toured west to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐遣征西將軍孔子等帥騎二萬擊契汗禿真於羅種。

translations.literal: King Qin Chiqian sent General Who Conquers the West Kongzi and others with twenty thousand cavalry to attack Qihan Tufa at Luozhong.
translations.idiomatic: King Qin Chiqian sent Kongzi, General Who Conquers the West, with twenty thousand horse against Qihan Tufa at Luozhong.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜所署晉昌太守唐契據郡叛，蒙遜遣世子政德討之。

translations.literal: Tang Qi, whom King of Hexi Meng Xun had appointed Governor of Jinchang, held the commandery in rebellion; Meng Xun sent his heir Zhengde to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qi, Meng Xun's appointee as Governor of Jinchang, rebelled and held the commandery; Meng Xun sent his heir Zhengde against him.

sentences.zh: 契，瑤之子也。

translations.literal: Qi was the son of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was the son of Yao.

sentences.zh: 上之為宋公也，謝瞻為宋台中書侍郎，其弟晦為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Duke of Song, Xie Zhan was Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat of the Song Terrace, and his younger brother Hui was General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu was Duke of Song, Xie Zhan was Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and his younger brother Hui was General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 時晦權遇已重，自彭城還都迎家，兵客輻湊，門巷填咽。

translations.literal: By then Hui's power and favor were already great; returning from Pengcheng to the capital to fetch his family, soldiers and clients crowded in such numbers that the lanes were choked.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hui's power was already great; returning from Pengcheng to fetch his family, his soldiers and clients packed the lanes until they could scarcely pass.

sentences.zh: 瞻在家，驚駭，謂晦曰：「汝名位未多，而人歸趣乃爾！

translations.literal: Zhan was at home and alarmed; he said to Hui: "Your rank and title are not yet great, yet people flock to you like this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was home and alarmed. He told Hui: "Your rank is not yet high, yet people flock to you like this!

sentences.zh: 吾家素以恬退為業，不願幹豫時事，交遊不過親朋。

translations.literal: Our family has always made quiet withdrawal its profession; we do not wish to meddle in current affairs, and our acquaintances extend no farther than kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Our family has always valued quiet withdrawal; we do not wish to meddle in affairs, and our circle extends no farther than kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 而汝遂勢傾朝野，此豈門戶之福邪！」

translations.literal: Yet you now tilt power across court and countryside—is this a blessing to our house!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you now dominate court and countryside—is this a blessing to our house!"

sentences.zh: 乃以籬隔門庭曰：「吾不忍見此。」

translations.literal: He then set up a fence to divide the courtyard and said: "I cannot bear to see this."
translations.idiomatic: He put up a fence across the courtyard and said: "I cannot bear to see this."

sentences.zh: 乃還彭城，言於宋公曰：「臣本素士，父祖位不過二千石。

translations.literal: He then returned to Pengcheng and said to the Duke of Song: "Your servant was originally a plain scholar; father and grandfather held posts no higher than two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Pengcheng and told the Duke of Song: "I was originally a plain scholar; my father and grandfather never rose above two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 弟年始三十，志用凡近，榮冠台府，位任顯密。

translations.literal: My brother is only thirty; his aims are ordinary, yet his honors crown the Terrace offices and his posts are conspicuous and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: My brother is only thirty, his talents ordinary, yet his honors crown the Terrace and his posts are weighty and exposed.

sentences.zh: 福過災生，其應無遠；

translations.literal: When fortune passes its measure, disaster is born—the response cannot be far off;
translations.idiomatic: When fortune exceeds its measure, disaster follows—the reckoning cannot be far off;

sentences.zh: 特乞降黜，以保衰門。」

translations.literal: I beg especially that he be demoted to preserve our declining house."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be demoted to preserve our house."

sentences.zh: 前後屢陳之。

translations.literal: He stated this repeatedly, before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded this again and again.

sentences.zh: 晦或以朝廷密事語瞻，瞻故向親舊陳說，用為戲笑，以絕其言。

translations.literal: Sometimes Hui would tell Zhan secret affairs of court; Zhan would deliberately repeat them to kin and friends as jest, to cut off such talk.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui confided court secrets, Zhan would repeat them to kin and friends as a joke, to stop such talk.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，晦以佐命功，位任益重，瞻愈憂懼。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Hui's merit as a founding supporter made his posts still weightier, and Zhan grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu took the throne, Hui's founding merit made his power still greater, and Zhan grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 是歲，瞻為豫章太守，遇病不療。

translations.literal: That year Zhan was Governor of Yuzhang; he fell ill and would not be treated.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhan was Governor of Yuzhang; he fell ill and refused treatment.

sentences.zh: 臨終，遺晦書曰：「吾得啟體幸全，亦何所恨！

translations.literal: On his deathbed he left Hui a letter saying: "I depart with body intact—what is there to regret!
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he wrote Hui: "I leave with body intact—what is there to regret!

sentences.zh: 弟思自勉勵，為國為家。」

translations.literal: Brother, strive to encourage yourself—for the state and for the family."
translations.idiomatic: Brother, strive on—for the state and for our family."

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝永初三年（

translations.literal: Third year of Yongchu of the High Ancestor Emperor Wu (
translations.idiomatic: Third year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu, the founding emperor (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元四二二年）

translations.literal: renxu, the year 422 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renxu, AD 422)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲辰朔，魏主自雲中西巡，至屋竇城。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, first day jiachen, the Wei ruler toured west from Yunzhong to Wudou City.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the first day jiachen, the Wei emperor toured west from Yunzhong to Wudou City.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以徐羨之為司空、錄尚書事，刺史如故；

translations.literal: Day guichou, Xu Xianzhi was made Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat, retaining his governorship;
translations.idiomatic: On day guichou Xu Xianzhi was made Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat, retaining his governorship;

sentences.zh: 江州刺史王弘為衛將軍、開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: Wang Hong, Governor of Jiangzhou, was made General of the Guard and Holder of the Grand Precedence;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, Governor of Jiangzhou, was made General of the Guard and Holder of the Grand Precedence;

sentences.zh: 中領軍謝晦為領軍將軍兼散騎常侍，入直殿省，總統宿衛。

translations.literal: Central Commander of the Army Xie Hui was made General of the Palace Army and concurrently Regular Attendant, entered attendance in the Palace Department, and took overall charge of the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, Central Commander of the Army, was made General of the Palace Army and Regular Attendant, entered attendance in the palace, and took charge of the night guard.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之起自布衣，又無術學，直以志力局度。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi had risen from common cloth and had no scholarly training; he relied solely on will, strength, and scope of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi had risen from common origins without scholarly training; he relied on will, force of character, and breadth of judgment.

sentences.zh: 一旦居廓廟，朝野推服，鹹謂有宰臣之望。

translations.literal: Once he stood in the great temple of state, court and countryside deferred to him; all said he had the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the highest office, court and country deferred to him; all said he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 沈密寡言，不以憂喜見色。

translations.literal: Deep and reserved, sparing of speech, he did not show joy or sorrow in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and reserved, he rarely spoke and never showed joy or sorrow on his face.

sentences.zh: 頗工弈棋，觀戲常若未解，當世倍以此推之。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled at chess; when watching games he often seemed not to understand, and his contemporaries doubled their esteem on that account.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at chess; when watching games he often seemed not to understand, and contemporaries esteemed him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 傅亮、蔡廓常言：「徐公曉萬事，安異同。」

translations.literal: Fu Liang and Cai Kuo often said: "Master Xu understands all affairs and settles differences."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang and Cai Kuo often said: "Master Xu understands everything and settles disputes."

sentences.zh: 嘗與傅亮、謝晦宴聚，亮、晦才學辯博，羨之風度詳整，時然後言。

translations.literal: Once at a banquet with Fu Liang and Xie Hui, Liang and Hui were learned and eloquent; Xianzhi's bearing was measured and complete, and he spoke only at the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet with Fu Liang and Xie Hui, Liang and Hui were learned and eloquent; Xianzhi's bearing was measured, and he spoke only when the moment required.

sentences.zh: 鄭鮮之歎曰：「觀徐、傅言論，不復以學問為長。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xianzhi sighed: "Watching Xu and Fu converse, one no longer takes learning as the chief excellence."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xianzhi sighed: "Watching Xu and Fu talk, one no longer thinks learning is what matters most."

sentences.zh: 秦征西將軍孔子等大破契汗禿真，獲男女二萬口，牛羊五十餘萬頭。

translations.literal: Qin's General Who Conquers the West Kongzi and others utterly defeated Qihan Tufa, taking twenty thousand men and women and more than five hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzi, Qin's General Who Conquers the West, routed Qihan Tufa, taking twenty thousand people and more than five hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 禿真帥騎數千西走，其別部樹奚帥戶五千降秦。

translations.literal: Tufa led several thousand horsemen west in flight; his separate division Shuxi led five thousand households in surrender to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa fled west with several thousand horse; his subordinate Shuxi surrendered with five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，詔分豫州淮以東為南豫州，治歷陽，以彭城王義康為刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, day dingchou, an edict divided the region east of the Huai in Yuzhou into Southern Yuzhou, with its seat at Liyang, and made Prince of Pengcheng Yikang its governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day dingchou, an edict split off the region east of the Huai as Southern Yuzhou, seat at Liyang, with Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as governor.

sentences.zh: 又分荊州十郡置湘州，治臨湘，以左衛將軍張邵為刺史。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were also set apart as Xiangzhou, with its seat at Linxiang, and General of the Left Guard Zhang Shao was made governor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were set apart as Xiangzhou, seat at Linxiang, with Zhang Shao, General of the Left Guard, as governor.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: Day bingxu, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingxu the Wei emperor returned to his palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，上不豫，太尉長沙王道憐、司空徐羨之、尚書僕射傅亮、領軍將軍謝晦、護軍將軍檀道濟並入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: Third month, the emperor was unwell; Grand Commandant Prince of Changsha Dao Lian, Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Vice Minister of the Secretariat Fu Liang, General of the Palace Army Xie Hui, and General Who Protects the Army Tan Daoji all entered to attend him with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor fell ill; Dao Lian, Prince of Changsha and Grand Commandant; Xu Xianzhi, Minister of Works; Fu Liang, Vice Minister of the Secretariat; Xie Hui, General of the Palace Army; and Tan Daoji, General Who Protects the Army, all attended him.

sentences.zh: 群臣請祈禱神祇，上不許，唯使侍中謝方明以疾告宗廟而已。

translations.literal: The ministers asked to pray to the spirits; the emperor would not permit it and only had Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Fangming report the illness to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to pray to the gods; the emperor refused and had Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Fangming report the illness to the ancestral temple only.

sentences.zh: 上性不信奇怪，微時多符瑞，及貴，史官審以所聞，上拒而不答。

translations.literal: By nature the emperor did not believe in strange things; in humble days there had been many portents, but when he rose high the historiographers carefully reported what they heard and he refused to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not believe in omens; in his humble days there had been many portents, but once he rose high he ignored what the historiographers reported.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟出為鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史，鎮廣陵，悉監淮南諸軍。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, stationed at Guangling, with overall supervision of all armies south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, stationed at Guangling with command of all forces south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 皇太子多狎群小，謝晦言於上曰：「陛下春秋既高，宜思存萬世，神器至重，不可使負荷非才。」

translations.literal: The crown prince often kept company with petty men. Xie Hui spoke to the emperor, saying: "Your Majesty's years are already advanced; you should think of preserving the realm for ten thousand generations. The sacred vessel is weighty indeed—it must not be borne by one without the talent for it."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince spent too much time with low companions. Xie Hui said to the emperor: "Your Majesty is growing old; you should think of securing the realm for generations to come. The throne is too weighty to rest on someone without the talent to bear it."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「廬陵何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How about Luling?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What of Luling?"

sentences.zh: 晦曰：「臣請觀焉。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "Your servant requests to observe him."
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied: "Let me go and see for myself."

sentences.zh: 出造廬陵王義真，義真盛欲與談，晦不甚答。

translations.literal: He went out to visit Prince of Luling Yizhen; Yizhen was eager to talk at length, but Hui did not respond much.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to call on Prince of Luling Yizhen, who was eager to talk at length, but Hui answered little.

sentences.zh: 還曰：「德輕於才，非人主也。」

translations.literal: Returning, he said: "His virtue is lighter than his talent—he is no ruler of men."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported: "His virtue falls short of his talent—he is not fit to be a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 丁未，出義真為都督南豫、豫、雍、司、秦、並六州諸軍事、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Yizhen was sent out as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for the six provinces Southern Yu, Yu, Yong, Si, Qin, and Bing; General of Chariots and Cavalry; with the Grand Duchy honorific of opening an office with equivalence to the Three Excellencies; and Governor of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingwei, Yizhen was posted out as commander of military affairs in Southern Yu, Yu, Yong, Si, Qin, and Bing; General of Chariots and Cavalry; with the Grand Duchy privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies; and Governor of Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 是後，大州率加都督，多者或至五十州，不可復詳載矣。

translations.literal: After this, great provinces generally had governors-general added; some reached as many as fifty provinces—they cannot all be recorded in detail here.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, large provinces were routinely placed under governors-general; some posts reached as many as fifty provinces, and the full list cannot be given here.

sentences.zh: 帝疾瘳，己未，大赦。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness improved; on day jiwei, a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness eased, a general amnesty was declared on day jiwei.

sentences.zh: 秦、雍流民南入梁州；

translations.literal: Refugees from Qin and Yong flowed south into Liangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Qin and Yong poured south into Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 庚申，遣使送絹萬匹，且漕荊、雍之谷以賑之。

translations.literal: on day gengshen, envoys were sent with ten thousand bolts of silk, and grain from Jing and Yong was transported by canal to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: on day gengshen the court sent envoys with ten thousand bolts of silk and shipped grain from Jing and Yong by canal to feed them.

sentences.zh: 刁逵之誅也，其子彌亡命。

translations.literal: When Diao Kui was executed, his son Mi fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: After Diao Kui was put to death, his son Mi went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，彌帥數十人入京口城，太尉留府司馬陸仲元擊斬之。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, Mi led several dozen men into Jingkou city; Lu Zhongyuan, acting chief administrator of the Grand Commandant's headquarters, attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinyou, Mi led several dozen men into Jingkou. Lu Zhongyuan, acting chief administrator at the Grand Commandant's headquarters, attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏河南王曜卒。

translations.literal: On day yichou, Prince of Henan Yao of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On day yichou, Yao, Prince of Henan in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲戌，魏立皇子燾為太平王，拜相國，加大將軍；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiaxu, Wei made the imperial son Tuo Prince of Taiping, appointed him Chancellor, and promoted him to Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day jiaxu, Wei made the imperial son Tuo Prince of Taiping, named him Chancellor, and promoted him to Grand General;

sentences.zh: 丕為樂平王，彌為安定王，范為樂安王，健為永昌王，崇為建寧王，俊為新興王。

translations.literal: Pi was made Prince of Leping, Mi Prince of Anding, Fan Prince of Le'an, Jian Prince of Yongchang, Chong Prince of Jianning, and Jun Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was made Prince of Leping, Mi Prince of Anding, Fan Prince of Le'an, Jian Prince of Yongchang, Chong Prince of Jianning, and Jun Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔封仇池公楊盛為武都王。

translations.literal: On day yihai, an edict enfeoffed Duke of Chouchi Yang Sheng as King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: On day yihai, an edict enfeoffed Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, as King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐以折衝將軍乞伏是辰為西胡校尉。

translations.literal: King of Qin Chiqian appointed General Who Breaks the Charge Qifu Shichen as Colonel of the Western Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: King Chiqian of Qin appointed Qifu Shichen, General Who Breaks the Charge, as Colonel of the Western Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 築列渾城於汁羅以鎮之。

translations.literal: He built Liehun Fort at Zhiruo to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He built Liehun Fort at Zhiruo to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝疾甚，召太子誡之曰：「檀道濟雖有干略，而無遠志，非如兄韶有難御之氣也。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the emperor's illness was severe; he summoned the crown prince and admonished him, saying: "Though Tan Daoji has capacity and strategy, he has no far-reaching ambition—not like your brother Shao, who has a spirit difficult to control.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor's illness grew grave. He summoned the crown prince and warned him: "Tan Daoji has talent and strategy, but no far-reaching ambition—not like your brother Shao, whose spirit is hard to restrain.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮，當無異圖。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang will surely harbor no divergent designs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang should have no designs of their own.

sentences.zh: 謝晦數從征伐，頗識機變，若有同異，必此人也。」

translations.literal: Xie Hui has repeatedly followed on campaign and knows well how to seize opportunities; if there is any disagreement, it will surely be this man."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui has campaigned with me many times and knows how to read a moment; if anyone turns against you, it will be he."

sentences.zh: 又為手詔曰：「後世若有幼主，朝事一委宰相，母后不煩臨朝。」

translations.literal: He also wrote a hand edict, saying: "If in later generations there is a young ruler, all court affairs shall be entrusted entirely to the chancellor; the empress dowager need not trouble herself to hold court."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a personal edict: "If a child ever succeeds to the throne, all court business shall go to the chancellor alone, and the empress dowager need not attend to government."

sentences.zh: 司空徐羨之、中書令傅亮、領軍將軍謝晦、鎮北將軍檀道濟同被顧命。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Secretariat Fu Liang, General of the Palace Army Xie Hui, and General Who Pacifies the North Tan Daoji were all entrusted with the regency.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Secretariat Fu Liang, General of the Palace Army Xie Hui, and General Who Pacifies the North Tan Daoji were all named regents.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝殂於西殿。

translations.literal: On day guihai, the emperor died in the Western Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On day guihai the emperor died in the Western Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝清簡寡慾，嚴整有法度，被服居處，儉於布素，游宴甚稀，嬪御至少。

translations.literal: The emperor was pure and simple, with few desires; stern and orderly, with law and measure. His dress and dwelling were economical, plainer than coarse cloth; banquets and feasts were very rare, and his consorts and attendants were very few.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lived plainly and with few desires, stern and disciplined. His dress and quarters were simpler than homespun; feasts were rare and his consorts few.

sentences.zh: 嘗得後秦高祖從女，有盛寵，頗以廢事；

translations.literal: Once he obtained a niece of the Later Qin Gaozu and favored her greatly, neglecting state affairs somewhat;
translations.idiomatic: Once he took a niece of Later Qin's founding emperor as a favorite and neglected affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 謝晦微諫，即時遣出。

translations.literal: Xie Hui remonstrated subtly, and the emperor immediately sent her away.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui remonstrated gently, and the emperor at once sent her away.

sentences.zh: 財帛皆在外府，內無私藏。

translations.literal: Treasure and cloth were all kept in the outer treasury; inside there was no private hoard.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and goods were kept in the public treasury; he kept no private store within the palace.

sentences.zh: 嶺南嘗獻入筒細布，一端八丈，帝惡其精麗勞人，即付有司彈太守，以布還之，並制嶺南禁作此布。

translations.literal: Lingnan once submitted tube-fine cloth—one bolt eight zhang. The emperor disliked its fineness and the labor it cost the people; he immediately handed it to the appropriate office to impeach the governor, returned the cloth, and decreed that Lingnan forbid making this cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan once sent tube-woven fine cloth, eight zhang to the bolt. The emperor hated its fineness and the labor it cost the people; he had the governor impeached, returned the cloth, and forbade Lingnan to make it.

sentences.zh: 公主出適，遣送不過二十萬，無錦繡之物。

translations.literal: When a princess went out in marriage, the send-off did not exceed two hundred thousand cash, with no brocade or embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: When a princess married out, her dowry never exceeded two hundred thousand cash and included no brocade or embroidery.

sentences.zh: 內外奉禁，莫敢為侈靡。

translations.literal: Within and without, all upheld the prohibition; none dared be extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace and out, all obeyed these restrictions, and none dared live lavishly.

sentences.zh: 太子即皇帝位，年十七，大赦，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，立妃司馬氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The crown prince assumed the imperial throne at age seventeen; a general amnesty was declared; the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager; Consort Sima was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took the throne at seventeen, declared a general amnesty, honored the empress dowager as grand empress dowager, and installed Lady Sima as empress.

sentences.zh: 後，晉恭帝女海鹽公主也。

translations.literal: The empress was the daughter of Emperor Gong of Jin, Princess of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: She was Princess of Haiyan, daughter of Emperor Gong of Jin.

sentences.zh: 魏主服寒食散，頻年藥發，災異屢見，頗以自憂。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler took cold-food powder; for years its effects flared up; portents appeared repeatedly, and he was much troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor took cold-food powder; for years its effects recurred, omens appeared again and again, and he grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 遣中使密問白馬公崔浩曰：「屬者日食趙、代之分。

translations.literal: He sent a palace envoy to inquire secretly of Duke of Baima Cui Hao, saying: "Recently there was an eclipse in the sectors of Zhao and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a palace envoy to consult Cui Hao, Duke of Baima, in secret: "Recently there was an eclipse over the Zhao and Dai regions.

sentences.zh: 朕疾彌年不愈，恐一旦不諱，諸子並少，將若之何？

translations.literal: My illness has gone on for years without cure; I fear that one day I may die suddenly; my sons are all still young—what shall be done?
translations.idiomatic: My illness has lingered for years without recovery. I fear I may die suddenly; my sons are all still young—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 其為我思身後之計。」

translations.literal: Think out a plan for me for after my death."
translations.idiomatic: Think out a plan for what comes after my death."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「陛下春秋富盛，行就平愈；

translations.literal: Hao said: "Your Majesty's years are in full vigor and you will soon be fully restored;
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied: "Your Majesty is still in the prime of life and will soon recover;

sentences.zh: 必不得已，請陳瞽言。

translations.literal: if it cannot be avoided, I beg leave to offer blind counsel.
translations.idiomatic: but if it must be said, I beg leave to offer blind counsel.

sentences.zh: 自聖代龍興，不崇儲貳，是以永興之始，社稷幾危。

translations.literal: Since our sacred dynasty rose like a dragon, we have not honored an heir apparent; thus at the beginning of Yongxing the altars of state nearly fell into peril.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty rose, we have not honored an heir apparent, and at the start of Yongxing the state nearly came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今宜早建東宮。

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Palace should be established early.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace should be established at once.

sentences.zh: 選賢公卿以為師傅，左右信臣以為賓友；

translations.literal: Choose worthy dukes and ministers as tutors, and trusted ministers at hand as companions;
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy ministers as tutors and trusted courtiers as companions;

sentences.zh: 入總萬機，出撫戎政。

translations.literal: let him take charge of all affairs within and oversee military policy without.
translations.idiomatic: let him manage all affairs within and military policy without.

sentences.zh: 如此，則陛下可以優遊無為，頤神養壽。

translations.literal: In this way Your Majesty may roam at ease in idleness, nourishing spirit and prolonging life.
translations.idiomatic: Then Your Majesty may rest at ease, tending your spirit and prolonging your years.

sentences.zh: 萬歲之後。

translations.literal: After ten thousand years,
translations.idiomatic: After ten thousand years,

sentences.zh: 國有成主，民有所歸，奸宄息望，禍無自生矣。

translations.literal: the state will have a fixed sovereign, the people will have one to whom to turn, traitors and evildoers will cease their hopes, and disaster will have no source from which to arise.
translations.idiomatic: the realm will have a settled ruler, the people a place to turn, traitors will abandon their hopes, and trouble will have no way to arise.

sentences.zh: 皇子燾年將周星，明睿溫和，立子以長，禮之大經，若必待成人然後擇之，倒錯天倫，則召亂之道也。」

translations.literal: The imperial son Tuo will soon complete his first year; he is bright, wise, gentle, and mild. To establish the eldest son is the great constant of ritual; if one must wait until adulthood before choosing, that inverts the proper order of human relations—the way that summons disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son Tuo will soon complete his first year; he is bright, wise, and gentle. To establish the eldest son is the great rule of ritual; to wait until adulthood before choosing would overturn the natural order and invite disorder."

sentences.zh: 魏主復以問南平公長孫嵩。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again put the question to Duke of Nanping Changsun Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor put the same question to Changsun Song, Duke of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「立長則順，置賢則人服；

translations.literal: He replied: "To establish the eldest is orderly; to install the worthy wins men's acceptance;
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "To establish the eldest is orderly; to install the worthy wins men's hearts;

sentences.zh: 燾長且賢，天所命也。」

translations.literal: Tuo is eldest and worthy—it is Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo is eldest and worthy—it is Heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，立太平王燾為皇太子，使之居正殿臨朝，為國副主。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice, installed Prince of Taiping Tuo as crown prince, had him dwell in the main hall and hold court, and made him deputy ruler of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, installed Prince of Taiping Tuo as crown prince, had him hold court in the main hall, and made him deputy ruler of the state.

sentences.zh: 以長孫嵩及山陽公奚斤、北新公安同為左輔，坐東廂，西面；

translations.literal: He made Changsun Song, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin, and Duke of Beixin An Tong left assistants; they sat in the eastern wing, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Changsun Song, Xi Jin, Duke of Shanyang, and An Tong, Duke of Beixin, as left assistants; they sat in the eastern wing, facing west;

sentences.zh: 崔浩與太尉穆觀、散騎常侍代人丘堆為右弼，坐西廂，東面；

translations.literal: Cui Hao, together with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Qiu Dui of Dai, were right assistants; they sat in the western wing, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, Grand Commandant Mu Guan, and Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Qiu Dui of Dai were right assistants; they sat in the western wing, facing east;

sentences.zh: 百官總己以聽焉。帝避居西宮，時隱而窺之，聽其決斷，大悅，謂侍臣曰：「嵩宿德舊臣，歷事四世，功存社稷；

translations.literal: All officials submitted their business to the crown prince for judgment. The emperor withdrew to the Western Palace; from time to time he hid himself and watched, listening to his decisions, and was greatly pleased. He said to the attending ministers: "Song is an old minister of long-standing virtue who has served through four reigns, whose achievements preserve the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: All officials submitted their business to the crown prince for judgment. The emperor withdrew to the Western Palace, sometimes hiding nearby to watch and listen to his decisions, and was greatly pleased. He told the attending ministers: "Song is an old minister of long standing who has served four reigns and whose service has preserved the state;

sentences.zh: 斤辯捷智謀，名聞遐邇；

translations.literal: Jin is eloquent, quick, and resourceful in stratagem, his name heard far and near;
translations.idiomatic: Jin is quick-witted and full of stratagem, his name known far and wide;

sentences.zh: 同曉解俗情，明練於事；

translations.literal: Tong understands worldly sentiment and is clear and practiced in affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Tong understands human affairs and is skilled in practical business;

sentences.zh: 觀達於政要，識吾旨趣；

translations.literal: Guan is versed in the essentials of government and knows my intent;
translations.idiomatic: Guan grasps the essentials of government and knows my mind;

sentences.zh: 浩博聞強識，精察天人；

translations.literal: Hao's learning is broad and his memory strong, with keen insight into Heaven and man;
translations.idiomatic: Hao's learning is vast and his memory strong, with keen insight into Heaven and man;

sentences.zh: 堆雖無大用，然在公專謹。

translations.literal: Though Dui has no great usefulness, in public he is single-minded and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dui lacks great talent, in office he is single-minded and careful.

sentences.zh: 以此六人輔相太子，吾與汝曹巡行四境，伐叛柔服，足以得志於天下矣。」

translations.literal: With these six men to assist and chancellor the crown prince, I and you all can tour the four borders, suppress rebellion and soothe submission, and that will suffice to achieve our will under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: With these six to assist the crown prince, I and you can tour the four borders, crush rebels and win over the submissive, and that will be enough to fulfill our ambitions under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 嵩實姓拔拔，斤姓達奚，觀姓丘穆陵，堆姓丘敦。

translations.literal: Song's original surname was Babba; Jin's was Daxi; Guan's was Qiumuling; Dui's was Qiudun.
translations.idiomatic: Song's original surname was Babba; Jin's was Daxi; Guan's was Qiumuling; Dui's was Qiudun.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏之群臣出於代北者，姓多重複，及高祖遷洛，始皆改之。

translations.literal: At this time, ministers of Wei who came from north of Dai had surnames often repeated and compound; when Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, they all began to change them.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Wei ministers from north of Dai often bore compound surnames; when Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, they all began to change them.

sentences.zh: 舊史患其煩雜難知，故皆從後姓以就簡易，今從之。

translations.literal: The old histories worried that this was tedious and hard to follow, so they all use the later surnames for simplicity; here we follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories found these names cumbersome and hard to follow, so they use the later surnames for simplicity; here we do the same.

sentences.zh: 魏主又以典東西部劉絜、門下奏事代人古弼、直郎徒河盧魯元忠謹恭勤，使之給侍東宮，分典機要，宣納辭令。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler also, because Liu Jie of the Eastern and Western Sections, Gu Bi of the Gates who presented memorials, and Lu Luyuan of Straight Lang were loyal, careful, and diligent, had them attend the Eastern Palace, divide and manage state secrets, and transmit and receive edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor also appointed Liu Jie of the Eastern and Western Sections, Gu Bi of the Gates who presented memorials, and Lu Luyuan of Straight Lang to attend the Eastern Palace because they were loyal and diligent; they shared control of state secrets and carried edicts in and out.

sentences.zh: 太子聰明，有大度。

translations.literal: The crown prince was intelligent and possessed great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was intelligent and broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 群臣時奏所疑，帝曰：「此非我所知，當決之汝曹國主也。」

translations.literal: When the ministers at times presented doubtful matters for decision, the emperor said: "This is not what I know—it should be decided by you, the ruler of the state."
translations.idiomatic: When ministers sometimes submitted doubtful matters, the emperor said: "This is not for me to decide—it should be settled by you, the ruler of the state."

sentences.zh: 六月，壬申，以尚書僕射傅亮為中書監、尚書令，以領軍將軍謝晦領中書令，侍中謝方明為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renshen, Vice Minister of the Secretariat Fu Liang was made Director of the Secretariat and Minister of the Secretariat; General of the Palace Army Xie Hui was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Fangming was made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day renshen, Fu Liang, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat and Minister of the Secretariat; Xie Hui, General of the Palace Army, was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; and Xie Fangming, Attendant-in-Ordinary, was made Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 方明善治郡，所至有能名；

translations.literal: Fangming was skilled at governing commanderies; wherever he went he won a reputation for competence;
translations.idiomatic: Fangming was skilled at governing commanderies and wherever he went earned a reputation for ability;

sentences.zh: 承代前人，不易其政，必宜改者，則以漸移變，使無跡可尋。

translations.literal: He inherited the work of his predecessors and did not change their policies; where change was necessary, he shifted things gradually so no trace could be detected.
translations.idiomatic: He took over from his predecessors without overturning their policies; where change was needed, he altered things gradually so no trace could be seen.

sentences.zh: 戊子，長沙景王道憐卒。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Prince of Changsha Jing Wang Dao Lian died.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuzi, Dao Lian, Prince of Changsha and posthumously honored as Jing, died.

sentences.zh: 魏建義將軍刁雍寇青州，州兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Diao Yong of Wei, General Who Establishes Righteousness, raided Qingzhou; the provincial troops defeated him.
