translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong of Wei, General Who Establishes Righteousness, raided Qingzhou, and the provincial troops defeated him.

sentences.zh: 雍收散卒。

translations.literal: Yong gathered his scattered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yong gathered his scattered troops.

sentences.zh: 走保大鄉山。

translations.literal: He fled and held out on Mount Daxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He fled and held out on Mount Daxiang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己酉，葬武皇帝於初寧陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou, Emperor Wu was buried at Chuning Mausoleum; temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day jiyou, Emperor Wu was buried at Chuning Mausoleum with the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜遣前將軍沮渠成都帥眾一萬，耀兵嶺南，遂屯五澗。

translations.literal: Meng Xun, King of Hexi, sent Forward General Juqu Chengdu leading ten thousand men to display military might south of the mountains, then encamped at Wujian.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun, King of Hexi, sent Forward General Juqu Chengdu with ten thousand men to show force south of the mountains, then encamped at Wujian.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦王熾磐遣征北將軍出連虔等騎六千擊之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, King of Qin Chiqian sent General Who Campaigns North Chu Lianqian and others with six thousand cavalry to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Chiqian of Qin sent General Who Campaigns North Chu Lianqian and others with six thousand cavalry to attack them.

sentences.zh: 初，魏主聞高祖克長安，大懼，遣使請和，自是每歲交聘不絕。

translations.literal: At first, when the Wei ruler heard that Gaozu had taken Chang'an, he was greatly afraid and sent envoys to sue for peace; from then on diplomatic exchanges each year never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the Wei emperor heard that Liu Yu had taken Chang'an, he was greatly alarmed and sent envoys to sue for peace; thereafter diplomatic exchanges never ceased from year to year.

sentences.zh: 及高祖殂，殿中將軍沈范等奉使在魏，還，及河，魏主遣人追執之，議發兵取洛陽、虎牢、滑台。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Palace General Shen Fan and others were on embassy in Wei; on their return, when they reached the river, the Wei ruler sent men in pursuit to seize them, and the court debated raising troops to take Luoyang, Hulao, and Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu died, Palace General Shen Fan and others were on embassy in Wei. On their return, when they reached the river, the Wei emperor sent men in pursuit to seize them, and the court debated sending troops to take Luoyang, Hulao, and Huatai.

sentences.zh: 崔浩諫曰：「陛下不以劉裕欻起，納其使貢，裕亦敬事陛下。

translations.literal: Cui Hao remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty, because Liu Yu rose suddenly, still received his envoys and tribute, and Yu also treated Your Majesty with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao remonstrated: "Your Majesty accepted Liu Yu's envoys and tribute even though he rose suddenly, and Liu Yu treated Your Majesty with respect in turn.

sentences.zh: 不幸今死，遽乘喪伐之，雖得之，不足為美。

translations.literal: Now that he has unhappily died, to rush at once to attack while the house is in mourning—even if you succeed, it is not a fair renown.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has died, to attack while the house is in mourning—even if you succeed, it will not be honorable.

sentences.zh: 且國家今日亦未能一舉取江南也，而徒有伐喪之名，竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: Moreover the state today is also not yet able to take Jiangnan in one stroke, yet you would merely gain the name of attacking a house in mourning—I privately deem this unworthy of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the state today cannot take Jiangnan in one stroke, yet you would gain only the name of attacking a house in mourning—I do not think this worthy of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜遣人弔祭，存其孤弱，恤其凶災，使義聲佈於天下，則江南不攻自服矣。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that you should send men to offer condolences and sacrifices, preserve his orphaned and weak, and relieve their disaster and mourning, so that righteous repute spreads through the realm—then Jiangnan will submit without attack.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that you should send envoys to offer condolences, protect the orphaned and weak, and relieve their grief, so that righteous repute spreads through the realm—then Jiangnan will submit without a fight.

sentences.zh: 況裕新死，黨與未離，兵臨其境，必相帥拒戰，功不可必。

translations.literal: Moreover Yu has just died; his faction has not yet dispersed; if troops press their borders, they will surely rally one another to resist—the outcome is not assured.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liu Yu has just died, his faction has not yet split, and if troops press their borders they will surely rally to resist—the outcome is not assured.

sentences.zh: 不如緩之，待其強臣爭權，變難必起，然後命將出帥，可以兵不疲勞，坐收淮北也。」

translations.literal: Better to bide your time and wait until his powerful ministers contend for power; strife is sure to arise; then you can order generals to take the field and can take Huaibei without weary troops."
translations.idiomatic: Better to wait until his powerful ministers contend for power and strife breaks out; then send generals into the field and take Huaibei without weary troops."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「劉裕乘姚興之死而滅之，今我乘裕喪而伐之，何為不可！」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "Liu Yu took advantage of Yao Xing's death to destroy him; now I take advantage of Yu's mourning to attack him—why should this not be done!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said: "Liu Yu seized on Yao Xing's death to destroy him; why should I not seize on Liu Yu's death to attack Song!"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 姚興死，諸子交爭，故裕乘釁伐之。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing died, his sons competed with one another; therefore Yu seized the opening to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing died, his sons fought one another, and Liu Yu seized the opening to attack.

sentences.zh: 今江南無釁，不可比也。」

translations.literal: Now there is no opening in Jiangnan—it cannot be compared."
translations.idiomatic: Now there is no such opening in Jiangnan—it is not the same."

sentences.zh: 魏主不從，假司空奚斤節，加晉兵大將軍、行揚州刺史，使督宋兵將軍、交州刺史周幾、吳兵將軍、廣州刺史公孫表同入寇。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler did not follow this advice; he granted acting Minister of Works Xi Jin the credential seal, added Grand General of Jin armies and acting Governor of Yangzhou, and had him supervise Song General Zhou Ji, Inspector of Jiao, and Wu General Gongsun Biao, Inspector of Guang, to invade together.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor would not listen. He granted Xi Jin, acting Minister of Works, the credential seal, promoted him to Grand General of Jin armies and acting Governor of Yangzhou, and had him lead Song General Zhou Ji, Inspector of Jiao, and Wu General Gongsun Biao, Inspector of Guang, in a joint invasion.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，魏主如灅南宮，遂如廣寧。

translations.literal: On day yisi, the Wei ruler went to Shuonan Palace, then to Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: On day yisi the Wei emperor went to Shuonan Palace, then on to Guangning.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏人築平城外郭，周圍三十二里。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the Wei people built the outer wall of Pingcheng, thirty-two li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinhai the Wei built the outer wall of Pingcheng, thirty-two li around.

sentences.zh: 魏主如喬山，遂東如幽州。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler went to Qiao Mountain, then east to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor went to Qiao Mountain, then east to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，還宮。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiaxu, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day jiaxu, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魏軍將發，公卿集議於監國之前，以先攻城與先略地。

translations.literal: When the Wei army was about to set out, dukes and ministers assembled in council before the regent crown prince, debating whether to attack cities first or seize territory first.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei army prepared to march, dukes and ministers assembled before the regent crown prince to debate whether to attack cities first or seize territory first.

sentences.zh: 奚斤欲先攻城，崔浩曰：「南人長於守城，昔苻氏攻襄陽，經年不拔。

translations.literal: Xi Jin wished to attack cities first; Cui Hao said: "Southerners excel at holding cities; in the past the Fu clan attacked Xiangyang and could not take it for a year.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin wanted to attack cities first. Cui Hao said: "Southerners excel at defense; when the Former Qin attacked Xiangyang, it could not be taken for a year.

sentences.zh: 今以大兵坐攻小城，若不時克，挫傷軍勢，敵得徐嚴而來，我怠彼銳，此危道也。

translations.literal: Now with a great army to sit and attack small cities—if they are not taken in time, army morale is wounded; the enemy can leisurely fortify and come; we grow weary while they grow sharp—this is a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: Now to sit a great army before small cities—if they are not taken quickly, morale suffers; the enemy can fortify at leisure and come against us weary while they are fresh. That is a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 不如分軍掄地，至淮為限，列置守宰，收斂租谷，則洛陽、滑台、虎牢更在軍北，絕望南救，必沿河東走；

translations.literal: Better to divide the army to sweep the land, with the Huai as limit, station governors and magistrates in array, collect rent grain—then Luoyang, Huatai, and Hulao lie further north of the army, cut off from southern rescue, and the enemy must flee east along the river;
translations.idiomatic: Better to divide the army and sweep the land as far as the Huai, station officials to collect grain and taxes—then Luoyang, Huatai, and Hulao will lie north of our army, cut off from southern relief, and the enemy must flee east along the river;

sentences.zh: 不則為囿中之物，何憂其不獲也！」

translations.literal: otherwise they become things within an enclosure—why worry that they will not be taken!"
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they become beasts in a pen—why worry that they cannot be taken!"

sentences.zh: 公孫表固請攻城，魏主從之。

translations.literal: Gongsun Biao firmly urged attacking cities, and the Wei ruler assented.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Biao pressed hard for attacking cities, and the Wei emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是奚斤等帥步騎二萬，濟河，營於滑台之東。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xi Jin and others led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry, crossed the river, and encamped east of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xi Jin and others led twenty thousand foot and horse, crossed the river, and encamped east of Huatai.

sentences.zh: 時司州刺史毛德祖戍虎牢，東郡太守王景度告急於德祖，德祖遣司馬翟廣等將步騎三千救之。

translations.literal: At this time Governor of Sizhou Mao Dezu was garrisoned at Hulao; Administrator of Dongjun Wang Jingdu reported urgency to Dezu, and Dezu sent the Major Zhai Guang and others with three thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Mao Dezu, governor of Sizhou, held Hulao; Wang Jingdu, administrator of Dongjun, sent Dezu an urgent appeal, and Dezu dispatched Major Zhai Guang and others with three thousand foot and horse to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 先是，司馬楚之聚眾在陳留之境，聞魏兵濟河，遣使迎降。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sima Chuzhi had gathered troops in the region of Chenliu; hearing that Wei troops had crossed the river, he sent an envoy to offer surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sima Chuzhi had gathered forces in the Chenliu region; when he heard Wei troops had crossed the river, he sent an envoy to submit.

sentences.zh: 魏以楚之為征南將軍、荊州刺史，使侵擾北境。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Chuzhi as General Who Conquers the South and Governor of Jingzhou, ordering him to raid the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei made Chuzhi General Who Conquers the South and governor of Jingzhou, and sent him to harass the northern border.

sentences.zh: 德祖遣長社令王法政將五百人戍邵陵，將軍劉憐將二百騎戍雍丘以備之。

translations.literal: Dezu sent the magistrate of Changshe Wang Fazheng with five hundred men to garrison Shaoling, and General Liu Lian with two hundred cavalry to garrison Yongqiu to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezu sent Wang Fazheng, magistrate of Changshe, with five hundred men to hold Shaoling, and General Liu Lian with two hundred horsemen to hold Yongqiu against him.

sentences.zh: 楚之引兵襲憐，不克。

translations.literal: Chuzhi led troops to attack Lian and did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi led troops against Lian but failed to break him.

sentences.zh: 會台送軍資，憐出迎之，酸棗民王玉馳以告魏。

translations.literal: When the platform sent military supplies, Lian went out to meet them; the commoner Wang Yu of Suanzao galloped to inform Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent military supplies, Lian went out to meet the convoy; Wang Yu, a commoner of Suanzao, rode posthaste to inform the Wei.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，魏尚書滑稽引兵襲倉垣，兵吏悉逾城走，陳留太守馮翊嚴稜詣斤降。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, the Wei Minister Huaji led troops to surprise Cangyuan; soldiers and officials all fled over the walls; Administrator of Chenliu Yan Ling of Fufeng went to Xi Jin and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingyou Minister Huaji of Wei led troops in a surprise attack on Cangyuan; the garrison fled over the walls; Yan Ling of Fufeng, administrator of Chenliu, went to Xi Jin and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 魏以王玉為陳留太守，給兵守倉垣。

translations.literal: Wei made Wang Yu Administrator of Chenliu and gave him troops to hold Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei appointed Wang Yu administrator of Chenliu and supplied troops to hold Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 奚斤等攻滑台，不拔，求益兵。

translations.literal: Xi Jin and others attacked Huatai but could not take it, and requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin and others besieged Huatai without success and asked for more troops.

sentences.zh: 魏主怒，切責之；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was angry and sharply rebuked them;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was furious and rebuked them sharply;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，自將諸國兵五萬餘人南出天關，逾恆嶺，為斤等聲援。

translations.literal: On day renchen, he personally led more than fifty thousand troops of the various states south out of Tianguan, crossed Heng Ridge, to support Xi Jin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: On day renchen he personally led more than fifty thousand troops from the federated states south through Tianguan, crossed Heng Ridge, to reinforce Xi Jin's forces.

sentences.zh: 秦出連虔與河西沮渠成都戰，禽之。

translations.literal: Qin general Chulian Qian fought with Juqu Chengdu of Hexi and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Chulian Qian fought Juqu Chengdu of Hexi and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏太子燾將兵出屯塞上，使安定王彌與安同居守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Wei crown prince Tao led troops out to encamp on the frontier, ordering Prince of Anding Ni and An Tong to remain and jointly guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Crown Prince Tao of Wei led troops to encamp on the frontier, leaving Prince Ni of Anding and An Tong to guard the capital together.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，奚斤等急攻滑台，拔之。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, Xi Jin and others pressed the attack on Huatai and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengxu Xi Jin and others pressed the attack on Huatai and captured it.

sentences.zh: 王景度出走；

translations.literal: Wang Jingdu fled in flight;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingdu fled;

sentences.zh: 景度司馬陽瓚為魏所執，不降而死。

translations.literal: Jingdu's Major Yang Zan was seized by Wei, would not surrender, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdu's major Yang Zan was captured by the Wei, refused to surrender, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 魏主以成皋侯苟兒為兗州刺史，鎮滑台。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler made Marquis of Chenggao Gou Er Governor of Yanzhou and stationed him at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor made Gou Er, Marquis of Chenggao, governor of Yanzhou and posted him at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 斤等進擊翟廣等於土樓，破之，乘勝進逼虎牢；

translations.literal: Xi Jin and others advanced to attack Zhai Guang and others at Tulou, defeated them, and pressing their victory advanced against Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: Jin's forces advanced against Zhai Guang and others at Tulou, routed them, and pressed on toward Hulao;

sentences.zh: 毛德祖與戰，屢破之。

translations.literal: Mao Dezu fought them and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu engaged them in battle and routed them again and again.

sentences.zh: 魏主別遣黑槊將軍於栗磾將三千人屯河陽，謀取金墉，德祖遣振威將軍竇晃等緣河拒之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler separately sent the Black Spear General Yu Libo with three thousand men to encamp at Heyang, planning to take Jinyong; Dezu sent the General Who Quells Might Dou Huang and others along the river to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor separately dispatched General Yu Libo of the Black Spear with three thousand men to encamp at Heyang, intending to seize Jinyong; Dezu sent General Dou Huang Who Quells Might and others to hold the river line against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，魏主至冀州，遣楚兵將軍、徐州刺史叔孫建將兵自平原濟河，徇青、兗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day bingxu, the Wei ruler reached Jizhou and sent the General of Chu Troops and Governor of Xuzhou Shusun Jian with troops to cross the river from Pingyuan and sweep Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day bingxu, the Wei emperor reached Jizhou and dispatched Shusun Jian, General of Chu Troops and governor of Xuzhou, to cross from Pingyuan and overrun Qing and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史劉粹遣治中高道瑾將步騎五百據項城，徐州刺史王仲德將兵屯湖陸。

translations.literal: Governor of Yuzhou Liu Cui sent the Chief Clerk Gao Daojin with five hundred infantry and cavalry to hold Xiangcheng; Governor of Xuzhou Wang Zhongde led troops to encamp at Huluo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cui, governor of Yuzhou, sent Chief Clerk Gao Daojin with five hundred foot and horse to hold Xiangcheng; Wang Zhongde, governor of Xuzhou, encamped at Huluo.

sentences.zh: 於栗磾濟河，與奚斤並力攻竇晃等，破之。

translations.literal: Yu Libo crossed the river and joined Xi Jin in combined attack on Dou Huang and others, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Libo crossed the river, joined Xi Jin, and together broke Dou Huang's force.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣中領軍代人娥清、期思侯柔然閭大肥將兵七千人會周幾、叔孫建南渡河，軍於碻磝。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent the Central Palace Guard Daiuren E Qing and Marquis of Qisi Rouran Lü Dafei with seven thousand troops to join Zhou Ji and Shusun Jian in crossing the river south, encamping at Qiao'ao.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent E Qing of the Dai clan, Central Palace Guard, and Lü Dafei, Marquis of Qisi of the Rouran, with seven thousand men to join Zhou Ji and Shusun Jian in crossing south, and encamped at Qiao'ao.

sentences.zh: 癸未，兗州刺史徐琰棄尹卯南走，於是泰山、高平、金鄉等郡皆沒於魏。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, Governor of Yanzhou Xu Yan abandoned Yimao and fled south; thereupon the commanderies of Taishan, Gaoping, Jinxiang, and others all fell to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On day guiwei Xu Yan, governor of Yanzhou, abandoned Yimao and fled south; Taishan, Gaoping, Jinxiang, and other commanderies thereupon fell to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建等東入青州，司馬愛之、季之先聚眾於濟東，皆降於魏。

translations.literal: Shusun Jian and others entered Qingzhou from the east; Sima Aizhi and Jizhi had earlier gathered troops east of the Ji, and all surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian and others pushed east into Qingzhou; Sima Aizhi and Jizhi, who had earlier gathered forces east of the Ji, all submitted to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏兵逼虎牢，青州刺史東莞竺夔鎮東陽城，遣使告急。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Wei troops pressed Hulao; Governor of Qingzhou Zhuhai Zhu Kui was stationed at Dongyang City and sent envoys reporting urgency.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuzi Wei troops pressed Hulao; Zhu Kui of Dongguan, governor of Qingzhou, held Dongyang City and sent an urgent appeal for help.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔南兗州刺史檀道濟監征討諸軍事，與王仲德共救之。

translations.literal: On day jichou, an edict appointed Governor of Nanyanzhou Tan Daoji to oversee the armies of campaign and suppression, to rescue together with Wang Zhongde.
translations.idiomatic: On day jichou an edict made Tan Daoji, governor of Nanyanzhou, director of the campaign armies, to join Wang Zhongde in the relief effort.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王義真遣龍驤將軍沈叔狸將三千人就劉粹，量宜赴援。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Yizhen sent the Flying Dragon General Shen Shuli with three thousand men to join Liu Cui, to go to the rescue as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yizhen of Luling sent General Shen Shuli of the Flying Dragon with three thousand men to Liu Cui's aid, to reinforce wherever need was greatest.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐征秦州牧曇達為左丞相、征東大將軍。

translations.literal: King Chi'pan of Qin appointed Governor of Qinzhou Tanda as Left Chancellor and Grand General Who Conquers the East.
translations.idiomatic: Chi'pan, king of Qin, appointed Tanda, governor of Qinzhou, Left Chancellor and Grand General Who Conquers the East.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝景平元年（

translations.literal: First year of Jingping of the High Ancestor Emperor Wu (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Jingping of Emperor Wu, the founding emperor (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元四二三年）

translations.literal: day guihai, CE 423)
translations.idiomatic: guihai, 423 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, new moon on day jihai, general amnesty, change of era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of day jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝禮南郊。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, the emperor performed rites at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinchou the emperor performed the suburban rites at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 魏于栗磾攻金墉，癸卯，河南太守王涓之棄城走。

translations.literal: Wei general Yu Libo attacked Jinyong; on day guimao, Administrator of Henan Wang Juanzhi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Libo of Wei attacked Jinyong; on day guimao Wang Juanzhi, administrator of Henan, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 魏主以栗磾為豫州刺史，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler made Libo Governor of Yuzhou and stationed him at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor made Libo governor of Yuzhou and posted him at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏主南巡垣岳，丙辰，至鄴。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler toured south to Yuanyue; on day bingchen, he reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor toured south to Yuanyue; on day bingchen he reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔征豫章太守蔡廓為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, an edict summoned Administrator of Yuzhang Cai Kuo to be Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiwei an edict summoned Cai Kuo, administrator of Yuzhang, to the post of Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廓謂傅亮曰：「選事若悉以見付，不論；

translations.literal: Kuo said to Fu Liang: "If the matters of selection are entirely entrusted to me, very well;
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said to Fu Liang: "If the entire business of appointments is entrusted to me, I have no objection;

sentences.zh: 不然，不能拜也。」

translations.literal: if not, I cannot accept the appointment."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I cannot accept the post."

sentences.zh: 亮以語錄尚書徐羨之，羨之曰：「黃、散以下悉以委蔡，吾徒不復措懷；

translations.literal: Liang reported this to Recording Secretary Xu Xianzhi; Xianzhi said: "For posts from Yellow Gate and Palace Attendant downward, all shall be entrusted to Cai; we need no longer concern ourselves;
translations.idiomatic: Liang repeated this to Xu Xianzhi, Recording Secretary; Xianzhi said: "From Palace Attendant and below, everything goes to Cai—we need not trouble ourselves further;

sentences.zh: 自此以上，故宜共參同異。」

translations.literal: from this level upward, it is proper that we jointly consider agreements and differences."
translations.idiomatic: for offices above that level, we should consult together on decisions."

sentences.zh: 廓曰：「我不能為塗干木署紙尾！」

translations.literal: Kuo said: "I cannot be Tu Ganmu signing at the foot of the paper!"
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said: "I will not be Ganmu Tu countersigning at the bottom of the dispatch!"

sentences.zh: 遂不拜。

translations.literal: He thereupon did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post.

sentences.zh: 干木，羨之小字也。

translations.literal: Ganmu was Xianzhi's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Ganmu was Xianzhi's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 選案黃紙，錄尚書與吏部沿書連名，教訓廓云然。

translations.literal: Appointment documents were on yellow paper; the Recording Secretary and the Ministry of Personnel signed in sequence on the same document—thus Xianzhi had instructed Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Appointment cases were written on yellow paper, with the Recording Secretary and the Ministry of Personnel signing in turn on the same document—this was what Xianzhi had told Kuo.

sentences.zh: 沈約論曰：「蔡廓固辭銓衡，恥為志屈；

translations.literal: Shen Yue's commentary says: "Cai Kuo firmly declined the scales of appointment, ashamed that his will should be bent;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue commented: "Cai Kuo firmly refused the post of Minister of Personnel, unwilling to bend his principles;

sentences.zh: 豈不知選、錄同體，義無偏斷乎！

translations.literal: did he not know that Selection and Recording are one body, and in principle there is no partial decision!
translations.idiomatic: Did he not know that the Ministry of Personnel and the Recording Secretary are one body, and that impartial judgment is impossible?

sentences.zh: 良以主暗時難，不欲居通塞之任。

translations.literal: Truly it was because the ruler was obscure and the times hard—he did not wish to hold an office of openings and closings.
translations.idiomatic: In truth the emperor was weak and the times treacherous—he did not wish to hold an office that decided who would pass and who would be blocked.

sentences.zh: 遠矣哉！」

translations.literal: How far-sighted!"
translations.idiomatic: How far he saw!"

sentences.zh: 庚申，檀道濟軍於彭城。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, Tan Daoji encamped at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengshen Tan Daoji took position at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏叔孫建入臨淄，所向城邑皆潰。

translations.literal: Shusun Jian of Wei entered Linzi; the cities he faced all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian of Wei entered Linzi; city after city fell before him.

sentences.zh: 竺夔聚民保東陽城，其不入城者，使各依據山險，芟夷禾稼。

translations.literal: Zhu Kui gathered the people to hold Dongyang City; those who did not enter the city he had each rely on mountain defiles, cutting down and destroying the grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kui gathered the people into Dongyang City; those who remained outside he sent to mountain fastnesses and had the grain crops destroyed.

sentences.zh: 魏軍至，無所得食。

translations.literal: When Wei troops arrived, they had nothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army arrived, it found nothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 濟南太守垣苗帥眾依夔。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jinan Yuan Miao led the masses to join Zhu Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Miao, administrator of Jinan, led his forces to join Zhu Kui.

sentences.zh: 刁雍見魏主於鄴，魏主曰：「叔孫建等入青州，民皆藏避，攻城不下。

translations.literal: Diao Yong had audience with the Wei ruler at Ye; the Wei ruler said: "Shusun Jian and others entered Qingzhou; the people all hid and fled; cities cannot be taken by assault.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong had audience with the Wei emperor at Ye; the emperor said: "Shusun Jian and others entered Qingzhou; the people all hid and fled; cities cannot be taken by assault.

sentences.zh: 彼素服卿威信，今遣卿助之。」

translations.literal: They have long respected your authority and trust; now I send you to assist them."
translations.idiomatic: They have long respected your authority; I now send you to assist them."

sentences.zh: 乃以雍為青州刺史，給雍騎，使行募兵以取青州。

translations.literal: He then made Yong Governor of Qingzhou, gave Yong cavalry, and had him recruit troops on the march to take Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Yong governor of Qingzhou, gave him cavalry, and had him recruit troops on the march to take Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏兵濟河向青州者凡六萬騎，刁雍募兵得五千人，撫慰士民，皆送租供軍。

translations.literal: Wei troops who crossed the river toward Qingzhou totaled sixty thousand cavalry; Diao Yong recruited five thousand men, comforted officials and people, and all sent rent to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei horsemen who crossed toward Qingzhou totaled sixty thousand; Diao Yong raised five thousand more, reassured the people, and all sent grain levies to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 柔然寇魏邊。

translations.literal: Rouran raided the Wei frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran raided the Wei border.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊辰，魏築長城，自赤城西至五原，延袤二千餘里，備置戍卒，以備柔然。

translations.literal: Second month, day wuchen, Wei built the Long Wall from west of Chicheng to Wuyuan, more than two thousand li in length, stationed frontier guards throughout, to guard against Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day wuchen, the Wei built the Great Wall from west of Chicheng to Wuyuan, more than two thousand li long, with garrisons stationed along it against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太皇太后蕭氏殂。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, the Grand Empress Dowager Lady Xiao died.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingchou the Grand Empress Dowager, Lady Xiao, died.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜及吐谷渾王阿柴皆遣使入貢。

translations.literal: King Mengsun of Hexi and King Acai of Tuyuhun both sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun, king of Hexi, and Acai, king of Tuyuhun, both sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔以蒙遜為都督涼、秦、河、沙四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、涼州牧、河西王；

translations.literal: On day gengchen, an edict made Mengsun Supervisor of Military Affairs for the four provinces of Liang, Qin, He, and Sha, General of Fast Cavalry, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Hexi;
translations.idiomatic: On day gengchen an edict made Mengsun supervisor of military affairs for Liang, Qin, He, and Sha, General of Fast Cavalry, governor of Liangzhou, and King of Hexi;

sentences.zh: 以阿柴為督塞表諸軍事、安西將軍、沙州刺史、澆河公。

translations.literal: Acai was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for the frontier passes, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Acai was made supervisor of frontier military affairs, General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬子，葬孝懿皇后於興寧陵。

translations.literal: Third month, day renzi, the Empress Xiaoyi was buried at Xingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day renzi, Empress Xiaoyi was interred at Xingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 魏奚斤、公孫表等共攻虎牢，魏主自鄴遣兵助之。

translations.literal: Xi Jin, Gongsun Biao, and others of Wei jointly attacked Hulao; the Wei ruler sent troops from Ye to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin, Gongsun Biao, and other Wei commanders jointly besieged Hulao; the Wei emperor sent reinforcements from Ye.

sentences.zh: 毛德祖於城內穴地入七丈，分為六道，出魏圍外；

translations.literal: Mao Dezu inside the city dug tunnels seven zhang deep, divided into six paths, exiting outside the Wei encirclement;
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city Mao Dezu dug tunnels seven zhang deep in six branches, emerging beyond the Wei lines;

sentences.zh: 募敢死之士四百人，使參軍范道基等帥之，從穴中出，掩襲其後。

translations.literal: he recruited four hundred dare-to-die warriors, had the aide Fan Daoji and others lead them, emerging from the tunnels to strike their rear by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: he raised four hundred volunteers for a death sortie, put Fan Daoji and other staff officers in command, and sent them through the tunnels to strike the Wei rear by surprise.

sentences.zh: 魏軍驚憂，斬首數百級，焚其攻具而還。

translations.literal: Wei troops were alarmed and unsettled; several hundred heads were cut off, siege engines were burned, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army panicked; the sortie took several hundred heads, burned the siege engines, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏兵雖退散，隨復更合，攻之益急。

translations.literal: Although Wei troops scattered and withdrew, they soon reassembled and attacked all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Wei forces scattered, they soon rallied and pressed the assault ever harder.

sentences.zh: 奚斤自虎牢將步騎三千，攻穎川太守李元德等於許昌，魏以穎川人庚龍為穎川太守，戍許昌。

translations.literal: Xi Jin led three thousand infantry and cavalry from Hulao to attack Governor of Yingchuan Li Yuande and others at Xuchang; Wei made Geng Long of Yingchuan Administrator of Yingchuan and garrisoned Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin led three thousand foot and horse from Hulao against Li Yuande, governor of Yingchuan, at Xuchang; the Wei installed Geng Long, a man of Yingchuan, as administrator there and garrisoned the city.

sentences.zh: 毛德祖出兵與公孫表大戰，從朝至晡，殺魏兵數百。

translations.literal: Mao Dezu led troops out to fight a great battle with Gongsun Biao, from morning until the hour of shen, killing several hundred Wei soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu marched out and fought Gongsun Biao from morning until evening, killing several hundred Wei soldiers.

sentences.zh: 會奚斤自許昌還，合擊德祖，大破之，亡甲士一千餘人，復嬰城自守。

translations.literal: When Xi Jin returned from Xuchang, they joined in attacking Dezu and routed him; more than a thousand armored soldiers were lost, and he again closed the city and held on alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Jin returned from Xuchang, the two commanders combined against Dezu and crushed him; he lost more than a thousand armored men and again shut the gates to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 魏主又遣萬餘人從白沙渡河，屯濮陽南。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again sent more than ten thousand men to cross the river from Baisha and encamp south of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent more than ten thousand men across the river at Baisha to encamp south of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 朝議以項城去魏不遠，非輕軍所抗，使劉粹召高道瑾還壽陽；

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Xiangcheng was not far from Wei and could not be resisted by a light force, and ordered Liu Cui to recall Gao Daojin to Shouyang;
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that Xiangcheng lay too close to the Wei for a small force to hold, and ordered Liu Cui to recall Gao Daojin to Shouyang;

sentences.zh: 若沈叔狸已進，亦宜且追。

translations.literal: if Shen Shuli had already advanced, he too should for the present be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: if Shen Shuli had already marched, he should be recalled as well.

sentences.zh: 粹奏：「虜攻虎牢，未復南向，若遽攝軍捨項城，則淮西諸郡無所憑依。

translations.literal: Cui memorialized: "The barbarians are attacking Hulao and have not yet turned south again; if we hastily withdraw the army and abandon Xiangcheng, the commanderies west of the Huai will have nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Cui memorialized: "The enemy is attacking Hulao and has not yet turned south again; if we hastily withdraw and abandon Xiangcheng, the commanderies west of the Huai will have nothing to rely on.

sentences.zh: 沈叔狸已頓肥口，又不宜遽退。」

translations.literal: Shen Shuli has already halted at Feikou; it is also inappropriate to withdraw hastily."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shuli has already halted at Feikou; a hasty withdrawal would be wrong as well."

sentences.zh: 時李元德帥散卒二百至項，劉粹使助高道瑾戍守，請宥其奔敗之罪，朝議並許之。

translations.literal: At this time Li Yuande led two hundred scattered soldiers to Xiang; Liu Cui had him assist Gao Daojin in the garrison, and requested pardon for his defeat and flight—the court discussion approved both.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Yuande led two hundred scattered soldiers to Xiangcheng; Liu Cui had him assist Gao Daojin in the garrison and asked pardon for his defeat and flight—the court approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 乙己，魏主畋於韓陵山，遂如汲郡，至枋頭。

translations.literal: On day yisi, the Wei ruler hunted at Hanling Mountain, then went to Jijun and reached Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: On day yisi the Wei emperor hunted at Hanling Mountain, then proceeded to Jijun and on to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 初，毛德祖在北，與公孫表有舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mao Dezu was in the north, he and Gongsun Biao had old ties.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Mao Dezu had been in the north, he and Gongsun Biao had been on friendly terms.

sentences.zh: 表有權略，德祖患之，乃與交通音問；

translations.literal: Biao had stratagems and resource; Dezu worried about this and therefore exchanged messages with him;
translations.idiomatic: Biao was wily and resourceful; Dezu, troubled by this, opened a secret correspondence with him;

sentences.zh: 密遣人說奚斤，雲表與之連謀。

translations.literal: secretly sending someone to tell Xi Jin that Biao was in league with him in a joint plot.
translations.idiomatic: and secretly sent word to Xi Jin that Biao was plotting with him.

sentences.zh: 每答表書，多所治定；

translations.literal: Each time he replied to Biao's letters, he revised them considerably;
translations.idiomatic: In every reply to Biao's letters he altered the wording at length;

sentences.zh: 表以書示斤，斤疑之，以告魏主。

translations.literal: Biao showed the letters to Xi Jin; Xi Jin grew suspicious and reported it to the Wei ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Biao showed the letters to Xi Jin; Xi Jin grew suspicious and reported the matter to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，表與太史令王亮少同營署，好輕侮亮；

translations.literal: Earlier, Biao and the Director of Astronomy Wang Liang had shared quarters in youth; he liked to slight Wang Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Biao and Wang Liang, Director of Astronomy, had served together in youth; Biao liked to slight him;

sentences.zh: 亮奏「表置軍虎牢東，不得便地，故令賊不時滅。」

translations.literal: Wang Liang memorialized: "Biao stationed the army east of Hulao in an unsuitable position, causing the bandits not to be destroyed in time."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang memorialized: "Biao had camped east of Hulao on unfavorable ground, delaying the destruction of the enemy."

sentences.zh: 魏主素好術數，以為然，積前後仇，使人夜就帳中縊殺之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler had always favored divination and arts of fate, believed it, added old and new grudges, and sent men by night into his tent to strangle him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor had always favored divination; he believed the charge, added old and new grudges together, and sent men by night into Biao's tent to strangle him.

sentences.zh: 乙卯。

translations.literal: On day yimao.
translations.idiomatic: On day yimao.

sentences.zh: 魏主濟自靈昌津，遂如東郡、陳留。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler crossed from Lingchang Ford, then went to Dongjun and Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor crossed at Lingchang Ford and proceeded to Dongjun and Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建將三萬騎逼東陽城，城中文武才一千五百人，竺夔、垣苗悉力固守，時出奇兵擊魏，破之。

translations.literal: Shusun Jian led thirty thousand cavalry to press Dongyang City; the civil and military within the city numbered only fifteen hundred; Zhu Kui and Yuan Miao strained every effort to hold firm, and from time to time sent surprise troops to strike Wei and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian led thirty thousand horsemen against Dongyang City; its garrison numbered only fifteen hundred civil and military officers; Zhu Kui and Yuan Miao defended with all their strength, sending out raiding parties from time to time to rout the Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏步騎繞城列陳十餘里，大治攻具。

translations.literal: Wei infantry and cavalry arrayed in camp around the city for more than ten li, greatly preparing siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Wei foot and horse encircled the city in battle lines more than ten li long and built siege engines on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 夔作四重塹，魏人填其三重，為□童車以攻城，夔遣人從地道中出，以大麻糸亙挽之令折。

translations.literal: Kui built four ditches in depth; the Wei filled three of them and built battering rams to attack the city; Kui sent men out from tunnels and with thick hemp ropes stretched across to snap them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kui dug four trenches; the Wei filled three and built battering rams for the assault; Zhu Kui sent men through tunnels to stretch heavy hemp ropes across them and snap them.

sentences.zh: 魏人復作長圍，長攻逾急。

translations.literal: The Wei again built a long encirclement; the prolonged assault grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei then built a full circumvallation, and the siege pressed ever harder.

sentences.zh: 歷時浸久，城轉墮壞，戰士多死傷，餘眾困乏，旦暮且陷。

translations.literal: As time lengthened, the walls gradually crumbled; many warriors were killed or wounded; the survivors were exhausted—morning or evening, and the city would fall.
translations.idiomatic: As weeks passed the walls began to give way; many defenders were killed or wounded; the survivors were exhausted and collapse seemed only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟至彭城，以司、青二州並急，而所領兵少，不足分赴；

translations.literal: Tan Daoji reached Pengcheng; because Sizhou and Qingzhou were both urgent but the troops he led were few and insufficient to divide and go to both;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji reached Pengcheng; both Sizhou and Qingzhou were in crisis, but his force was too small to split;

sentences.zh: 青州道近，竺夔兵弱，乃與王仲德兼行先救之。

translations.literal: the road to Qingzhou was near and Zhu Kui's troops were weak; he therefore went together with Wang Zhongde to rescue there first.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou was closer and Zhu Kui's force was weaker, so he and Wang Zhongde pressed ahead together to relieve it first.

sentences.zh: 甲子，劉粹遣李元德襲許昌，斬庾龍。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, Liu Cui sent Li Yuande to raid Xuchang and beheaded Yu Long.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiazi, Liu Cui sent Li Yuande to strike Xuchang and killed Yu Long.

sentences.zh: 元德因留綏撫，並上租糧。

translations.literal: Yuande thereupon remained to pacify and comfort the people, and also forwarded rent grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande stayed on to pacify the region and sent up the collected rent grain.

sentences.zh: 魏主至盟津。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler arrived at Mengjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor reached Mengjin.

sentences.zh: 於栗磾造浮橋於冶阪津。

translations.literal: Yuliudu built a pontoon bridge at Yebankou Crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliudu built a pontoon bridge at the Yebankou ford.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏主引兵北濟，西如河內。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the Wei ruler led his army north across the river and west toward Henei.
translations.idiomatic: On day yichou the Wei emperor led his troops north across the Yellow River and west toward Henei.

sentences.zh: 娥清、周幾、閭大肥徇地至湖陸、高平，民屯聚而射之。

translations.literal: E Qing, Zhou Ji, and Lü Dafei ranged over the land as far as Hulu and Gaoping; the people gathered in camps and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: E Qing, Zhou Ji, and Lü Dafei raided as far as Hulu and Gaoping, where local militias gathered and fired on them.

sentences.zh: 清等盡攻破高平諸縣，滅數千家，虜掠萬餘口；

translations.literal: Qing and the others completely overran the counties of Gaoping, destroying several thousand households and carrying off more than ten thousand people;
translations.idiomatic: Qing and his colleagues overran the counties around Gaoping, wiping out several thousand households and carrying off more than ten thousand people;

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史鄭順之戍湖陸，以兵少不敢出。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Zheng Shunzhi garrisoned Hulu but, having too few troops, did not dare sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Inspector Zheng Shunzhi held Hulu but dared not come out, his force being too small.

sentences.zh: 魏主又遣并州刺史伊樓拔助奚斤攻虎牢。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again sent Bingzhou Inspector Yilou Ba to assist Xi Jin in attacking Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor also sent Bingzhou Inspector Yilou Ba to reinforce Xi Jin's assault on Hulao.

sentences.zh: 毛德祖隨方抗拒，頗殺魏兵，而將士稍零落。

translations.literal: Mao Dezu resisted as occasion demanded and killed quite a few Wei soldiers, but his officers and men gradually dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu met each attack as it came and killed many Wei soldiers, but his garrison slowly thinned.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁卯，魏主如成皋，絕虎牢汲河之路。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day dingmao, the Wei ruler went to Chenggao and cut off Hulao's route to the Ji River.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day dingmao the Wei emperor went to Chenggao and severed Hulao's supply line to the Ji River.

sentences.zh: 停三日，自督眾攻城，竟不能下，遂如洛陽觀《石經》。

translations.literal: He halted three days, personally supervised the masses in storming the city, yet in the end could not take it, and then went to Luoyang to view the Stone Classics.
translations.idiomatic: After three days he personally directed the assault on the city but still could not take it, so he proceeded to Luoyang to view the Stone Classics.

sentences.zh: 遣使祀嵩高。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to offer sacrifice to Songgao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to sacrifice at Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建攻東陽，墮其北城三十許步。

translations.literal: Shusun Jian attacked Dongyang and breached its northern wall by some thirty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian attacked Dongyang and broke down some thirty paces of the northern wall.

sentences.zh: 刁雍請速入，建不許，遂不克。

translations.literal: Diao Yong asked to enter at once; Jian would not permit it, and so they failed to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong urged a quick entry, but Jian refused, and the assault failed.

sentences.zh: 及聞檀道濟等將至，雍又謂建曰：「賊畏官軍突騎，以鎖連車為函陳。

translations.literal: When he heard that Tan Daoji and the others were about to arrive, Yong again said to Jian: "The enemy fear the government army's shock cavalry and have chained their wagons together into a box formation.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Tan Daoji and the others were approaching, Yong again told Jian, "The enemy fear our shock cavalry and have chained their wagons into a fortified wagon encampment.

sentences.zh: 大峴已南，處處狹隘，車不得方軌。

translations.literal: South of Great Xian, the way is narrow everywhere and wagons cannot run abreast.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Great Xian Pass the road is narrow everywhere, and wagons cannot travel side by side.

sentences.zh: 雍請將所募兵五千據險以邀之，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Yong asked to lead the five thousand men he had recruited to hold the defiles and intercept them; victory would be certain."
translations.idiomatic: Let me take the five thousand men I have raised and hold the defiles to ambush them—we are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 時天暑，魏軍多疫。

translations.literal: At that time the weather was hot and many in the Wei army were stricken with plague.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was sweltering, and plague had spread widely through the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 建曰：「兵人疫病過半，若相持不休，兵自死盡，何須復戰！

translations.literal: Jian said: "More than half the soldiers are sick with plague; if we keep up a stalemate without end, the troops will die off on their own—what need is there to fight again!
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "More than half the men are sick with plague. If we keep this up, the army will die away on its own—why fight at all!

sentences.zh: 今全軍而返，計之上也。」

translations.literal: To withdraw the whole army now is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: The best course now is to withdraw the whole army intact."

sentences.zh: 己巳，道濟軍於臨朐。

translations.literal: On day jisi, Daoji's army was at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: On day jisi Tan Daoji's army reached Linqu.

sentences.zh: 壬申，建等燒營及器械而遁；道濟至東陽，糧盡，不能追。

translations.literal: On day renshen Jian and the others burned their camp and equipment and fled. Daoji reached Dongyang, but his grain was exhausted and he could not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: On day renshen Jian and the others burned their camp and equipment and withdrew. Tan Daoji reached Dongyang, but with his supplies exhausted he could not pursue.

sentences.zh: 竺夔以東陽城壞，不可守，移鎮不其城。

translations.literal: Zhu Kui, because Dongyang's walls were ruined and the city could not be held, moved his headquarters to Buqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kui, finding Dongyang's walls too ruined to defend, shifted his headquarters to Buqi.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建自東陽趨滑台，道濟分遣王促德向尹卯。

translations.literal: Shusun Jian hurried from Dongyang toward Huatai; Daoji separately sent Wang Zhongde toward Yimao.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian marched from Dongyang toward Huatai, while Tan Daoji detached Wang Zhongde toward Yimao.

sentences.zh: 道濟停軍湖陸，仲德未至尹卯，聞魏兵已遠，還就道濟。

translations.literal: Daoji halted his army at Hulu; Zhongde had not yet reached Yimao when he heard the Wei army was already far off and returned to join Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji halted at Hulu. Before Zhongde reached Yimao he learned the Wei forces were already far away and turned back to rejoin Tan Daoji.

sentences.zh: 刁雍遂留鎮尹卯，招集譙、梁、彭、沛民五千餘家，置二十七營以領之。

translations.literal: Diao Yong thereupon remained to garrison Yimao, gathering more than five thousand households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei and establishing twenty-seven camps to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong stayed to garrison Yimao, gathering more than five thousand households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei and organizing them into twenty-seven camps.

sentences.zh: 蠻王梅安帥渠帥數十人入貢於魏。

translations.literal: The Man king Mei An led several dozen chieftains to enter and pay tribute to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Man king Mei An led several dozen tribal chieftains to Wei to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，諸蠻本居江、淮之間，其後種落滋蔓，佈於數州，東連壽春，西通巴、蜀，北接汝、穎，往往有之。

translations.literal: Earlier the various Man peoples originally dwelt between the Yangzi and Huai; afterward their clans spread and multiplied, spreading through several provinces—east to Shouchun, west connecting with Ba and Shu, north touching Ru and Ying—until they were found everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Man peoples had lived between the Yangzi and Huai, but their clans later spread through several provinces, reaching east to Shouchun, west into Ba and Shu, and north into the Ru and Ying regions, until they were found almost everywhere.

sentences.zh: 在魏世不甚為患；

translations.literal: In the Wei era they were not much of a trouble;
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei they had not been much of a threat;

sentences.zh: 及晉，稍益繁昌，漸為寇暴。

translations.literal: by Jin they gradually grew more numerous and flourishing and slowly became raiders and plunderers.
translations.idiomatic: under Jin they grew more numerous and gradually turned to raiding and plunder.

sentences.zh: 及劉、石亂中原，諸蠻無所忌憚，漸復北徙，伊闕以南，滿於山谷矣。

translations.literal: When the Liu and Shi regimes threw the Central Plains into chaos, the various Man had nothing to fear and gradually moved north again; south of Yique the valleys were full of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu and Shi regimes threw the Central Plains into chaos, the Man no longer had anything to fear and drifted north again until the valleys south of Yique were full of them.

sentences.zh: 河西世子政德攻晉昌，克之。

translations.literal: The heir of Hexi, Zhengde, attacked Jinchang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde, heir apparent of Hexi, attacked Jinchang and captured it.

sentences.zh: 唐契及弟和、甥李寶同奔伊吾，招集遺民，歸附者至二千餘家，臣於柔然；

translations.literal: Tang Qi, his brother He, and his nephew Li Bao fled together to Yiwu, gathered displaced people, and those who submitted reached more than two thousand households; they became subjects of Rouran;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qi, his brother He, and his nephew Li Bao fled together to Yiwu, gathered displaced people, and won the allegiance of more than two thousand households, submitting to Rouran;

sentences.zh: 柔然以契為伊吾王。

translations.literal: Rouran made Qi king of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran made Tang Qi king of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐謂其群臣曰：「今宋雖奄有江南，夏人雄據關中，皆不足與也。

translations.literal: King of Qin Chiqian said to his ministers: "Now although Song holds all the lands south of the Yangzi and the Xia people dominate Guanzhong, neither is worth matching ourselves against.
translations.idiomatic: King Chiqian of Qin told his ministers, "Song may now hold all the south, and Xia dominate Guanzhong, but neither is worth our concern.

sentences.zh: 獨魏主奕世英武，賢能為用，且讖云『恆代之北當有真人』，吾將舉國而事之。」

translations.literal: Only the Wei ruler, heroic and martial through generations, employs the worthy and able; moreover a prophecy says, 'North of Hengdai there shall be a true man.' I shall devote the whole state to serving him."
translations.idiomatic: Only the Wei emperor, heroic through generations and skilled at employing talent, is worth serving—and a prophecy says, 'North of Hengdai there shall be a true lord.' I mean to submit the whole state to him."

sentences.zh: 乃遣尚書郎漠者阿胡等入見於魏，貢黃金二百斤，並陳伐夏方略。

translations.literal: He then sent Secretariat Gentleman Moze Ahu and others to enter and have audience with Wei, presenting two hundred jin of gold and also setting forth a strategy for attacking Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Secretariat Gentleman Moze Ahu and others to audience with Wei, presenting two hundred jin of gold and outlining a plan for attacking Xia.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁未，魏主如河內，登太行，至高都。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day dingwei, the Wei ruler went to Henei, ascended the Taihang Mountains, and reached Gaodu.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on day dingwei the Wei emperor went to Henei, crossed the Taihang Mountains, and reached Gaodu.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建自滑台西就奚斤，共入虎牢。

translations.literal: Shusun Jian went west from Huatai to join Xi Jin, and together they entered Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian marched west from Huatai to join Xi Jin, and together they pressed into Hulao.

sentences.zh: 虎牢被圍二百日，無日不戰，勁兵戰死殆盡，而魏增兵轉多。

translations.literal: Hulao had been besieged two hundred days; not a day passed without fighting; the crack troops were nearly all killed in battle, while Wei kept sending more reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Hulao had been under siege for two hundred days without a day free of fighting. Its best troops were nearly all dead, while Wei kept sending fresh reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 魏人毀其外城，毛德祖於其內更築三重城以拒之，魏人又毀其二重。

translations.literal: The Wei men destroyed the outer wall; inside it Mao Dezu built three more walls to resist them, and the Wei men destroyed two of those as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei tore down the outer wall, so Mao Dezu built three inner walls in its place; the Wei destroyed two of those as well.

sentences.zh: 德祖唯保一城，晝夜相拒，將士眼皆生創。

translations.literal: Dezu held only one wall left, resisting day and night; the officers' and soldiers' eyes all developed sores.
translations.idiomatic: Dezu held out in the one remaining wall, fighting day and night until every officer and soldier had sores around his eyes from exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 德祖撫之以恩，終無離心。

translations.literal: Dezu treated them with kindness and grace, and in the end none lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Dezu treated them with kindness, and in the end none wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時檀道濟軍湖陸，劉粹軍項城，沈叔狸軍高橋，皆畏魏兵強，不敢進。

translations.literal: At this time Tan Daoji's army was at Hulu, Liu Cui's at Xiangcheng, and Shen Shuli's at Gaoqiao; all feared the Wei army's strength and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji was encamped at Hulu, Liu Cui at Xiangcheng, and Shen Shuli at Gaoqiao, but all feared the Wei forces and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏人作地道以洩虎牢城中井，井深四十丈，山勢峻峭，不可得防；

translations.literal: On day dingsi the Wei men dug tunnels to drain the wells in Hulao city; the wells were forty zhang deep and the mountainside steep and precipitous, so there was no way to guard against it;
translations.idiomatic: On day dingsi the Wei dug tunnels to drain Hulao's wells. The wells were forty zhang deep and the terrain too steep to defend;

sentences.zh: 城中人馬渴乏，被創者不復出血，重以饑疫，魏仍急攻之，己未，城陷。

translations.literal: The men and horses in the city were parched and exhausted; the wounded no longer bled; added to this were famine and plague; Wei still pressed the attack fiercely, and on day jiwei the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Men and horses inside were parched with thirst, the wounded no longer bled, and famine and plague compounded their misery. Wei pressed the attack hard, and on day jiwei the city fell.

sentences.zh: 將士欲扶德祖出走。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers wished to support Dezu and flee.
translations.idiomatic: His officers and men wanted to help Dezu escape.

sentences.zh: 德祖曰：「我誓與此城俱斃，義不使城亡而身存也！」

translations.literal: Dezu said: "I swear to perish together with this city; by right I cannot let the city fall while I remain alive!"
translations.idiomatic: Dezu said, "I have sworn to die with this city. I cannot in honor let the city fall while I live!"

sentences.zh: 魏主命將士；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered the officers and soldiers:
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered his troops:

sentences.zh: 「得德祖者，必生致之。」

translations.literal: "Whoever captures Dezu must bring him alive."
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever captures Dezu must bring him in alive."

sentences.zh: 將軍代人豆代田執德祖以獻。

translations.literal: The general Dou Daitian of Dai seized Dezu and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: General Dou Daitian of Dai seized Dezu and presented him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 將佐在城中者，皆為魏所虜，唯參軍范道基將二百人突圍南還。

translations.literal: The officers and aides who had been in the city were all captured by Wei; only Army Aide Fan Daoji led two hundred men in a breakout south and returned.
translations.idiomatic: All the officers and aides in the city were taken by Wei; only Army Aide Fan Daoji broke out south with two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 魏士座卒疫死者亦什二三。

translations.literal: Of the Wei soldiers, one or two in ten also died of plague.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Wei troops as well, one or two in ten died of plague.

sentences.zh: 奚斤等悉定司、兗、豫諸郡縣，置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: Xi Jin and the others completely settled the commanderies and counties of Si, Yan, and Yu, appointing governors and magistrates to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin and his colleagues pacified the commanderies and counties of Si, Yan, and Yu, appointing local officials to govern them.

sentences.zh: 魏主命周幾鎮河南，河南人安之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Zhou Ji to garrison Henan; the people of Henan were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor posted Zhou Ji to garrison Henan, and the people there were reassured.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮、謝晦以亡失境土，上表自劾；

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui, because territory had been lost, submitted memorials impeaching themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui memorialized to impeach themselves for the lost territory;

sentences.zh: 詔勿問。

translations.literal: an edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: an edict told them to disregard the matter.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之兄子吳郡太守珮之頗豫政事，與侍中王韶之、程道惠、中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛結為黨友。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi's elder brother's son Pei Zhi, Administrator of Wu Commandery, took part rather much in state affairs and formed a clique with Palace Attendant Wang Shaozhi, Cheng Daohui, Secretariat Drafter Xing Antai, and Pan Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi's nephew Pei Zhi, administrator of Wu Commandery, had grown deeply involved in court affairs and formed a faction with Palace Attendant Wang Shaozhi, Cheng Daohui, Secretariat Drafter Xing Antai, and Pan Sheng.

sentences.zh: 時謝晦久病，不堪見客，珮之等疑其詐疾，有異圖，乃稱羨之意以告傅亮，欲令亮作詔誅之。

translations.literal: At this time Xie Hui had long been ill and could not bear to receive visitors; Pei Zhi and the others suspected he was feigning sickness and harbored a different design, and so, claiming it was Xianzhi's wish, they told Fu Liang and wanted Liang to draft an edict to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui had long been ill and could not receive visitors. Pei Zhi and the others suspected he was feigning sickness and plotting treason, and claiming to speak for Xianzhi they urged Fu Liang to draft an edict ordering his execution.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「我等三人同受顧命，豈可自相誅戮！

translations.literal: Liang said: "We three received the same dying charge—how can we slaughter one another!
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "We three received the same deathbed charge—how can we turn on one another!

sentences.zh: 諸君果行此事，亮當角巾步出掖門耳。」

translations.literal: If you gentlemen truly carry this out, Liang will put on a scholar's headcloth and walk out the Side Gate."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly do this, I shall put on a commoner's headcloth and walk out the palace side gate."

sentences.zh: 珮之等乃止。

translations.literal: Pei Zhi and the others thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi and the others then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，己亥，魏宜都文成王穆觀卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day jihai, Prince Wencheng of Yidu of Wei, Mu Guan, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day jihai Prince Wencheng of Yidu, Mu Guan, died.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，魏主北巡，至參合陂。

translations.literal: On day bingchen the Wei ruler toured north and reached Canhe Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingchen the Wei emperor toured north as far as Canhe Marsh.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉，尊帝母張夫人為皇太后。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on day guiyou, the emperor's mother Lady Zhang was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day guiyou the emperor's mother, Lady Zhang, was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 魏主如三會屋侯泉。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler went to Sanhui Wuhou Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor went to Sanhui Wuhou Spring.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑，如馬邑，觀灅源。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day xinchou, he went to Mayi and viewed Lei Source.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day xinchou he went to Mayi and visited Lei Source.

sentences.zh: 柔然寇河西，河西王蒙遜命世子政德擊之。

translations.literal: Rouran raided Hexi; the King of Hexi, Mengxun, ordered the heir Zhengde to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran raided Hexi, and King Mengxun of Hexi ordered his heir Zhengde to repel them.

sentences.zh: 政德輕騎進戰，為柔然所殺，蒙遜立次子興為世子。

translations.literal: Zhengde advanced with light cavalry to give battle and was killed by Rouran; Mengxun established his second son Xing as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde charged ahead with light cavalry and was killed by Rouran. Mengxun then named his second son Xing heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙亥，魏主還宮，召奚斤還平城，留兵守虎牢；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day yihai, the Wei ruler returned to the palace, summoned Xi Jin back to Pingcheng, and left troops to guard Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on day yihai the Wei emperor returned to court, recalled Xi Jin to Pingcheng, and left troops to hold Hulao;

sentences.zh: 使娥清、周幾鎮枋頭；

translations.literal: he sent E Qing and Zhou Ji to garrison Fangtou;
translations.idiomatic: he posted E Qing and Zhou Ji at Fangtou;

sentences.zh: 以司馬楚之所將戶口置汝南、南陽、南頓、新蔡四郡，以益豫州。

translations.literal: the households led by Sima Chuzhi were settled in the four commanderies of Runan, Nanyang, Nandun, and Xincai to augment Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: the people Sima Chuzhi had led were settled in the four new commanderies of Runan, Nanyang, Nandun, and Xincai to enlarge Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸卯，魏人廣西宮外垣，週二十里。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day guimao, the Wei people expanded the outer wall of the Western Palace, twenty li in circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day guimao the Wei expanded the outer wall of the Western Palace to a circuit of twenty li.

sentences.zh: 禿髮辱檀之死也，河西王蒙遜遣人誘其故太子虎台，許以番禾、西安二郡處之，且借之兵，使伐秦，報其父仇，復取故地。

translations.literal: When Tufa Rutan died, the King of Hexi, Mengxun, sent men to entice his former crown prince Hutai, promising to settle him in the two commanderies of Fanhe and Xi'an and also to lend him troops to attack Qin, avenge his father's death, and recover his former lands.
translations.idiomatic: After Tufa Rutan's death, King Mengxun of Hexi sent envoys to entice his former crown prince Hutai, promising him the two commanderies of Fanhe and Xi'an and troops to attack Qin, avenge his father, and recover his old lands.

sentences.zh: 虎台陰許之，事洩而止。

translations.literal: Hutai secretly agreed, but when the affair leaked out it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hutai secretly agreed, but the plot leaked and came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐之後，虎台之妹也，熾磐待之如初。

translations.literal: Empress Hou was a younger sister of Hutai and a consort of King of Qin Chiqian; Chiqian treated her as before.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hou was Hutai's sister and a consort of King Chiqian of Qin, who continued to treat her as before.

sentences.zh: 後密與虎台謀曰：「秦本我之仇讎，雖以婚姻待之，蓋時宜耳。

translations.literal: The empress secretly plotted with Hutai and said: "Qin was originally our sworn enemy; although they treat us with marriage ties, that is only because the times require it.
translations.idiomatic: In secret she plotted with Hutai and said, "Qin has always been our enemy. Their courtesy through marriage is only a matter of expedience.

sentences.zh: 先王之薨，又非天命。

translations.literal: Our late king's death was moreover not Heaven's decree.
translations.idiomatic: Our late king's death was no act of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遺令不治者，欲全濟子孫故也。

translations.literal: The testament not to pursue vengeance was because he wished to preserve and save his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He left orders not to seek revenge only to preserve his descendants.

sentences.zh: 為人子者，豈可臣妾於仇讎而不思報復乎！」

translations.literal: As someone's child, how can one serve the enemy as subject and concubine and not think of revenge!"
translations.idiomatic: As his children, how can we serve our enemy and never think of vengeance!"

sentences.zh: 乃與武衛將軍越質洛城謀弒熾磐。

translations.literal: She then joined Palace Guard General Yuezhi Luocheng in plotting to assassinate Chiqian.
translations.idiomatic: She then joined Palace Guard General Yuezhi Luocheng in a plot to assassinate Chiqian.

sentences.zh: 後妹為熾磐左夫人，有寵，知其謀而告之，熾磐殺後及虎台等十餘人。

translations.literal: Empress Hou's younger sister was Chiqian's Left Lady and was favored; she learned of the plot and reported it, and Chiqian executed Hou and Hutai and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hou's younger sister, Chiqian's favored Left Lady, learned of the plot and reported it. Chiqian executed Hou, Hutai, and more than ten others.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏周幾寇許昌，許昌潰，穎川太守李元德奔項。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zhou Ji of Wei raided Xuchang; Xuchang collapsed, and Yingchuan Administrator Li Yuande fled to Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhou Ji of Wei raided Xuchang. The city fell, and Yingchuan Administrator Li Yuande fled to Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏人圍汝陽，汝陽太守王公度亦奔項。

translations.literal: On day wuchen the Wei men besieged Ruyang; Ruyang Administrator Wang Gongdu also fled to Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuchen the Wei besieged Ruyang, and Ruyang Administrator Wang Gongdu also fled to Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 劉粹遣其將姚聳夫等將兵助守項城。

translations.literal: Liu Cui sent his generals Yao Songfu and others to lead troops to help defend Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cui sent his generals Yao Songfu and others with troops to help hold Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏人夷許昌城，毀鐘城，以立封疆而還。

translations.literal: The Wei men razed Xuchang city, destroyed Zhongcheng, established the border demarcation, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei razed Xuchang, destroyed Zhongcheng, marked out their new frontier, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 己巳，魏太宗殂。

translations.literal: On day jisi Emperor Taizong of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On day jisi Emperor Mingyuan of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 壬申，世祖即位，大赦。

translations.literal: On day renshen the Shizu emperor ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On day renshen Emperor Taiwu ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，魏葬明元帝於金陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day gengzi, Wei buried Emperor Mingyuan at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day gengzi Wei buried Emperor Mingyuan at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 廟號太宗。

translations.literal: His temple name was Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: His temple name was Taizong.

sentences.zh: 魏主追尊其母杜貴嬪為密皇后。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler posthumously honored his mother, Lady Du the Noble Consort, as Empress Mi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor posthumously honored his mother, Noble Consort Du, as Empress Mi.

sentences.zh: 自司徒長孫嵩以下普增爵位。

translations.literal: From Grand Minister Changsun Song downward, ranks of nobility were universally raised.
translations.idiomatic: From Grand Minister Changsun Song downward, noble ranks were raised across the board.

sentences.zh: 以襄城公盧魯元為中書監，會稽公劉為尚書令，司衛監尉眷、散騎侍郎劉庫仁等八人分典四部。

translations.literal: Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan was made Director of the Secretariat; Duke of Kuaiji Liu was made Director of the Department of State Affairs; Palace Guard Director Yu Juan, Palace Attendant Gentleman Liu Kuren, and eight others in all were assigned to administer the four bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luyuan, Duke of Xiangcheng, was made Director of the Secretariat; Liu, Duke of Kuaiji, was made Director of the Department of State Affairs; and Yu Juan, Director of the Palace Guard, Liu Kuren, Gentleman of the Palace Attendant Office, and six others were assigned to oversee the four bureaus.

sentences.zh: 眷，古真之弟子也。

translations.literal: Juan was a disciple of Guzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Juan was a disciple of Guzhen.

sentences.zh: 以河內鎮將代人羅結為侍中，、外都大官，總三十六曹事。

translations.literal: Luo Jie of Dai, garrison commander of Henei, was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Inner and Outer Palace Affairs, overseeing the affairs of the thirty-six offices.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jie of Dai, garrison commander of Henei, was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Inner and Outer Palace Affairs, with authority over all thirty-six offices.

sentences.zh: 結時年一百七，精爽不衰，魏主以其忠愨，親任之，使兼長秋卿，監典後宮，出入臥內；

translations.literal: Jie was then one hundred seven years old, his spirit undiminished; the Wei ruler, because of his loyalty and sincerity, personally entrusted him, making him also Director of the Palace Domestic Service to supervise the inner palace, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Jie was then one hundred seven and still keen in mind. The Wei emperor trusted him for his loyalty and made him also Director of the Palace Domestic Service to oversee the inner palace, with access even to the imperial sleeping quarters;

sentences.zh: 年一百一十，乃聽歸老，朝廷每有大事，遣騎訪焉；

translations.literal: at one hundred ten he was permitted to retire; whenever the court had a great matter, it sent riders to consult him;
translations.idiomatic: at one hundred ten he was allowed to retire, yet whenever the court faced a major decision it sent riders to consult him;

sentences.zh: 又十年乃卒。

translations.literal: ten years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: he lived ten years more and then died.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫崔浩研精經術，練習制度，凡朝廷禮儀，軍國書詔，無不關掌。

translations.literal: Left Grandee of the Palace Cui Hao had mastered the classics and trained in institutions; all court ritual and state and military documents and edicts were under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, Left Grandee of the Palace, had mastered the classics and state institutions; court ritual and all civil and military documents passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 浩不好老、莊之書，曰：「此矯誣之說，不近人情。

translations.literal: Hao disliked the books of Laozi and Zhuangzi and said: "These are deceitful doctrines, remote from human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Hao disliked Laozi and Zhuangzi and said: "These are deceitful doctrines, remote from human nature.

sentences.zh: 老聃習禮，仲尼所師，豈肯為敗法之書以亂先王之治乎！」

translations.literal: Old Dan studied ritual and was teacher to Zhongni—how could he have written books to ruin the law and disorder the governance of the former kings!"
translations.idiomatic: Laozi studied ritual and was Confucius's teacher—how could he have written books to subvert the law and overturn the rule of the ancient kings!"

sentences.zh: 尤不信佛法，曰：「何為事此胡神！」

translations.literal: He especially did not believe in Buddhism and said: "Why serve this barbarian god!"
translations.idiomatic: He especially rejected Buddhism and said: "Why serve this foreign god!"

sentences.zh: 及世祖即位，左右多毀之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, those around him often slandered Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, courtiers often slandered him.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，命浩以公歸第。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to order Hao to retire to his mansion with ducal rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to send Hao home with ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 然素知其賢，每有疑議，輒召問之。

translations.literal: Yet he had long known Hao's worth; whenever there was a doubtful matter he would summon and question him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had long known Hao's worth; whenever a question arose he still summoned him.

sentences.zh: 浩纖妍潔白如美婦人，常自謂才比張良，而稽古過之。

translations.literal: Hao was slender, fair, and white as a beautiful woman; he often said his talent matched Zhang Liang's and that in mastery of antiquity he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was slender and fair as a beautiful woman; he often likened himself to Zhang Liang and claimed to surpass him in learning from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 既歸第，因修服食養性之術。

translations.literal: After returning home he took up the arts of diet and nurturing life.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring he took up dietary and longevity practices.

sentences.zh: 初，嵩山道士寇謙之，贊之弟也，修張道陵之術，自言嘗遇老子降，命謙之繼道陵為天師，授以辟谷輕身之術及《科戒》二十卷，使之清整道教。

translations.literal: Earlier the Daoist of Mount Song Kou Qianzhi, younger brother of Zan, practiced the arts of Zhang Daoling; he said he had once met Laozi descending, who ordered Qianzhi to succeed Daoling as Celestial Master, gave him the arts of grain avoidance and lightening the body and twenty scrolls of Regulations and Admonitions, and charged him to purify and order the Way of the Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kou Qianzhi, a Daoist of Mount Song and younger brother of Zan, practiced Zhang Daoling's teachings. He claimed Laozi had descended and named him Celestial Master in Daoling's line, taught him fasting and lightness of body, gave him twenty scrolls of Regulations and Admonitions, and charged him to reform the Daoist church.

sentences.zh: 又遇神人李譜文，雲老子之玄孫也，授以《圖菉真經》六十餘卷，使之輔佐北方太平真君；

translations.literal: He also met the divine man Li Puwen, said to be Laozi's great-great-grandson, who gave him more than sixty scrolls of the True Scripture of Charts and Registers and charged him to assist the Perfect Lord of Northern Great Peace;
translations.idiomatic: He also met the divine man Li Puwen, said to be Laozi's descendant, who gave him more than sixty scrolls of the True Scripture of Charts and Registers and charged him to assist the Perfect Lord of Northern Great Peace;

sentences.zh: 出天宮靜輪之法，其中數篇，李君之手筆也。

translations.literal: and revealed the method of the Heavenly Palace's Still Wheel; several sections were in Master Li's own hand.
translations.idiomatic: and revealed the method of the Heavenly Palace's Still Wheel, several sections in Master Li's own hand.

sentences.zh: 謙之奉其書獻於魏主。

translations.literal: Qianzhi presented these books to the Wei ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi presented these writings to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 朝野多未之信，崔浩獨師事之，從受其術，且上書贊明其事曰：「臣聞聖王受命，必有天應。

translations.literal: Court and countryside mostly did not believe; Cui Hao alone took him as master, received his arts, and memorialized in praise: "Your servant has heard that when a sage king receives the mandate, Heaven must respond.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country mostly disbelieved; Cui Hao alone became his disciple, learned his arts, and memorialized: "I have heard that when a sage king receives the mandate, Heaven responds.

sentences.zh: 《河圖》、《洛書》皆寄言於蟲獸之文，未若今日人神接對，手笑粲然，辭旨深妙，自古無比。

translations.literal: The River Chart and Luo Writings both conveyed their message through the markings of insects and beasts—nothing like today, when man and god meet face to face, hands laughing bright, words profound and subtle, unmatched since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The River Chart and Luo Writings spoke through the marks of beasts—nothing like today, when man and god meet face to face with radiant smiles, in words profound and unmatched since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 豈可以世俗常慮而忽上靈之命！

translations.literal: How can one with ordinary worldly scruples neglect the command of the spirits above!
translations.idiomatic: How can ordinary worldly caution ignore the command of the spirits above!

sentences.zh: 臣竊懼之。」

translations.literal: Your servant privately fears this."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this deeply."

sentences.zh: 帝欣然，使謁都奉玉帛、牲牢祭嵩岳，迎致謙之弟子在山中者，以崇奉天師，顯揚新法，宣佈天下。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and had the Director of Visitors offer jade and silk and sacrificial animals at Mount Song, summon Qianzhi's disciples still in the mountains, honor the Celestial Master, proclaim the new law, and announce it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and sent offerings to Mount Song, summoned Qianzhi's disciples from the mountains, honored the Celestial Master, proclaimed the new law, and announced it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 起天師道場於平城之東南，重壇五層，給道士百二十人衣食，每月設廚會數千人。

translations.literal: A Celestial Master ritual ground was built southeast of Pingcheng with a five-tiered altar; one hundred twenty Daoists were supplied with food and clothing, and each month kitchen feasts were held for several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: A Celestial Master ritual ground was built southeast of Pingcheng with a five-tiered altar; one hundred twenty Daoists were supported, and monthly feasts fed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：老、莊之書，大指欲同死生，輕去就。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang remarks: The books of Laozi and Zhuangzi aim chiefly to equate life and death and to treat going and staying lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang writes: Laozi and Zhuangzi chiefly aim to equate life and death and treat advancement and withdrawal lightly.

sentences.zh: 而為神仙者，服餌修煉以求輕舉，煉草石為金銀，其為術正相戾矣。

translations.literal: Those who seek to become immortals ingest elixirs and refine themselves to rise lightly, smelting plants and stones into gold and silver—their arts directly contradict this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who seek immortality ingest elixirs and refine themselves to ascend lightly, transmuting plants and stones into gold and silver—arts that directly contradict this.

sentences.zh: 是以劉歆《七略》敘道家為諸子，神仙為方技。

translations.literal: Therefore in Liu Xin's Seven Summaries the Daoist school is classed among the philosophers and immortals among the technical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Liu Xin's Seven Summaries classed the Daoists among philosophers and immortals among technical arts.

sentences.zh: 其後復有符水、禁咒之術，至謙之遂合而為一；

translations.literal: Later came the arts of talisman water and forbidden incantations, and with Qianzhi they were merged into one;
translations.idiomatic: Later came talisman water and incantations, and Qianzhi merged them into one;

sentences.zh: 至今循之，其訛甚矣！

translations.literal: and to this day they are followed—the error is very great!
translations.idiomatic: and they are followed to this day—a grave corruption!

sentences.zh: 崔浩不喜佛、老之書而信謙之之言，其故何哉！

translations.literal: Cui Hao disliked Buddhist and Laozhuang books yet believed Qianzhi's words—what was the reason!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao rejected Buddhism and Laozi-Zhuangzi yet believed Qianzhi—why!

sentences.zh: 昔臧文仲祀爰居，孔子以為不智；

translations.literal: In antiquity Zang Wenzhong sacrificed to Aiju; Confucius deemed this unwise;
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Wenzhong sacrificed to the seabird Aiju, Confucius called it unwise;

sentences.zh: 如謙之者，其為爰居亦大矣。

translations.literal: as for one like Qianzhi, his Aiju is even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's error is far greater than Aiju.

sentences.zh: 「《詩》三百，一言以蔽之，曰思無邪。」

translations.literal: "The three hundred poems of the Odes may be summed in one phrase: Think without evil."
translations.idiomatic: "The three hundred poems may be summed in one phrase: Think without evil."

sentences.zh: 君子之於擇術，可不慎哉！

translations.literal: How careful must the gentleman be in choosing his arts!
translations.idiomatic: How careful must a gentleman be in choosing his path!
